[Q1019] Hardly had I stepped out of the house [than it started raining].

(a) when it started raining

(c) than it had started raining

[SOL]
'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is always followed by 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. Hence, 'when it started raining' is the correct replacement.

[Q1020] She is [more taller than] her sister by two inches.

(a) taller than

[SOL]

[Q1021] Neither the teacher nor the students [was'] in the class room.

(a) were
(b) are
(c) have been
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject ('the students'). Since 'students' is plural, the plural verb 'were' is required.

[Q1022] If I [was you], I would never accept such treatment.

(a) were you
(b) am you
(c) have been you
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary or unreal situation, 'were' is used with all subjects, not 'was'. Hence, 'were you' is correct.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive mood) में सभी कर्ता के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।

[Q1023] The train [had left] before we reached the station.

(a) left

[ANS] d

In past time clauses with 'before', the earlier action takes Past Perfect ('had left') and the later action takes Simple Past ('reached'). The sentence is already grammatically correct.

[Q1024] Each of the players [were given] a medal for their performance.

[Q1028] If no substitution is required, select 'No improvement'. He **did not know how to solving** the complex mathematical problem.

[Q1029] She **has not and cannot be** pardoned for her grave misconduct.

(a) has not and cannot be
(b) has not and can never be
(c) has not been and cannot be
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
When two auxiliary verbs share a common main verb, both must be grammatically complete. 'Has not' requires 'been' before the past participle 'pardoned'. Hence, 'has not been and cannot be' is correct.
उदा. जब दो auxiliary verbs एक ही main verb के साथ प्रयोग हों, तो दोनों व्याकरणिक रूप से पूर्ण होने चाहिए। 'has not been' सही संयोजन है।
[RULE] Parallelism and Auxiliary Verbs

[Q1030] Neither of the two candidates **have paid** their subscription.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) have paid
(b) has paid
(c) have pay
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Neither of' takes a singular verb because it refers to each one individually. Thus, 'has paid' should replace 'have paid'.
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद plural noun आता है लेकिन verb हमेशा singular होती है। इसलिए 'has paid' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement

---

[Q1031] Scarcely had I got off the train **than** a group of coolies rushed towards me.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) than
(b) when
(c) then
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'Scarcely' or 'Hardly' is 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. Therefore, 'when' is correct.
उदा. 'Scarcely' या 'Hardly' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'than' का नहीं (than का प्रयोग 'No sooner' के साथ होता है)।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions

---

[Q1032] If you **would have read** the instructions carefully, you would not have answered wrongly.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) would have read
(b) had read
(c) have read
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In a third conditional sentence expressing a past hypothetical condition, the 'if' clause must be in the past perfect tense ('had + V3'), not 'would have'. Hence, 'had read' is correct.
उदा. Conditional sentence के नियम के अनुसार 'If + had + V3' के साथ 'would have + V3' का प्रयोग होता है। इसलिए 'had read' सही है।
[RULE] Conditional Sentences (Type 3)

---

[Q1033] The manager told the staff that **each of them should thoroughly check their work** before submission.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) each of them should thoroughly check their work
(b) each of them should thoroughly check his work
(c) each of them should thoroughly check our work
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When 'each' is used as a pronoun, the corresponding possessive pronoun/adjective in standard traditional grammar is masculine singular ('his') unless the gender is specifically feminine. Thus, 'his work' is grammatically preferred in SSC exams.
उदा. 'Each' के साथ singular possessive pronoun ('his') का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Pronoun Agreement

---

[Q1034] Despite of his hard work, **he could not succeed** in the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) he could not succeed
(b) he could not succeeded
(c) he cannot succeed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The preposition 'Despite' is never followed by 'of' (unlike 'In spite of'). The rest of the clause 'he could not succeed' is grammatically correct as modal verbs are followed by V1.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता (जबकि 'In spite of' होता है)। शेष वाक्य सही है।
[RULE] Prepositions and Modals

---

[Q1035] He is looking forward **to meet his family** after a long gap of five years.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to meet his family
(b) to meeting his family
(c) for meeting his family
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrasal verb/idiomatic expression 'look forward to' is always followed by a gerund (V1+ing), not a bare infinitive. Therefore, 'to meeting' is correct.
उदा. 'Look forward to' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V1+ing) का प्रयोग होता है, न कि infinitive का।
[RULE] Gerunds after Specific Prepositional Phrases

---

[Q1036] Not only the principal **but also the teachers was** present at the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) but also the teachers was
(b) but also the teachers were
(c) but the teachers was
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When subjects are joined by 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, 'the teachers' is plural, so the plural verb 'were' must be used.
उदा. 'Not only... but also' से जुड़े वाक्यों में verb अपने सबसे पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है। 'teachers' plural है, अतः 'were' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Correlatives)

[Q1037] No sooner did the train stop at the platform **when the passengers rushed** towards the doors.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when the passengers rushed
(b) than the passengers rushed
(c) then the passengers rushed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'No sooner' is always followed by the conjunction 'than', not 'when'. Hence, 'than the passengers rushed' is the correct substitution.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग होता है, 'when' का नहीं।
[RULE] Conjunction Pairing with No Sooner

[Q1038] The committee will convene at the next meeting to discuss the ___ for the upcoming project.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) plans
(b) proposal
(c) arrangements
(d) scheme
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The noun ‘proposal’ is the most appropriate collocation with ‘discuss’ and ‘project’. The other options either do not fit the context or are less precise.
उदा. ‘proposal’ is a formal term for a plan presented for discussion.
[RULE] Appropriate noun collocation with verb ‘discuss’

[Q1039] The new law has been enacted to ___ the rights of the vulnerable.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) protect
(b) preserve
(c) safeguard
(d) guard
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb ‘protect’ directly follows the preposition ‘to’ and correctly conveys the intent of the law. ‘Preserve’ and ‘safeguard’ are acceptable but ‘protect’ is the most commonly used in legal contexts.
उदा. ‘protect’ is used frequently in legislation.
[RULE] Verb choice after ‘to’ in infinitive form

[Q1040] She was praised for ___ her excellent performance in the exam.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) giving
(b) giving up
(c) giving of
(d) giving in
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase ‘for giving’ is idiomatic when referring to a reward or praise. The other options are incorrect prepositional phrases.
उदा. ‘for giving’ is the standard construction.
[RULE] Idiomatic prepositional phrase with ‘for’

[Q1041] The manager advised the team to ___ any doubts before the present at i on.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) clarify
(b) clarifying
(c) clarifies
(d) clarified
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The infinitive ‘to clarify’ follows the verb ‘advise’ correctly. The other options are wrong verb forms.
उदा. ‘advise’ is followed by an infinitive.
[RULE] Verb ‘advise’ followed by infinitive

[Q1042] The government will announce the new policy next week, ___ it will be implemented immediately.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) when
(b) whenever
(c) how
(d) where
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The adverb ‘when’ correctly links the two clauses about timing. ‘Whenever’ implies any time, which is not suitable here.
उदा. ‘when’ is used to express a specific time.
[RULE] Use of adverb ‘when’ to connect clauses

[Q1043] The students were asked to ___ their essays before the final submission.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) review
(b) reviewed
(c) reviewing
(d) reviews
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The infinitive ‘to review’ is required after ‘asked to’. The other options are incorrect verb forms.
उदा. ‘asked to’ is followed by an infinitive.
[RULE] Infinitive after ‘asked to’

[Q1044] The researcher emphasized the need for ___ data from multiple sources.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) collecting
(b) collection
(c) collected
(d) collects
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The noun ‘collection’ correctly follows ‘need for’. ‘Collecting’ would be a gerund but ‘collection’ is more appropriate in this context.
उदा. ‘need for collection’ is a standard phrase.
[RULE] Noun following ‘need for’

[Q1045] The project will be completed by the end of the year, ___ the team will start the next phase.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) afterwards
(b) otherwise
(c) hence
(d) therefore
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The adverb ‘therefore’ correctly indicates a logical consequence. ‘Afterwards’ indicates a later time, not a consequence.
उदा. ‘therefore’ is used to show result.
[RULE] Use of adverb ‘therefore’ for logical consequence

[Q1046] The committee will provide a detailed report, ___ the management will review it thoroughly.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) so
(b) so that
(c) stated
(d) saying
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The conjunction ‘so that’ introduces purpose; it is the correct connector for the intended meaning. ‘So’ alone does not convey purpose.
उदा. ‘so that’ is used to express purpose.

[Q1047] The assignment requires students to ___ their research findings in a written report.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) present
(b) presented
(c) presenting
(d) presentation
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The infinitive ‘to present’ follows ‘requires’. The other options are incorrect verb forms.
उदा. ‘requires’ is followed by an infinitive.
[RULE] Infinitive after ‘requires’

[Q1048] The manager, [who had previously overseen similar projects], was assigned to the new venture.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]

(a) who has previously overseen similar projects
(b) who had previously overseen similar projects
(c) who previously had overseen similar projects
(d) who previously oversee similar projects
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrase is a restrictive relative clause that modifies 'manager'. It should use the past perfect tense to refer to an earlier action.
उदा. "जैसा कि पहले प्रबंधक ने इसी तरह के प्रोजेक्ट्स की निगरानी की थी…"

[Q1049] The committee will review the proposal after receiving the final report, [by the dead line
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) by the deadline
(b) by deadline
(c) by the deadlines
(d) by deadline's
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The prepositional phrase should be 'by the deadline' to indicate the time constraint.
उदा. "समय सीमा के भीतर"
[RULE] Prepositional Phrase of Time

[Q1050] She has been working on the project, [which has earned her recognition].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which has earned her recognition
(b) which earned her recognition
(c) which has earning her recognition
(d) Zealous
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative clause requires the present perfect tense to link the action to the present.
उदा. "जिसने उसे मान्यता दिलाई है…"
[RULE] Relative Clause with Present Perfect

[Q1051] The team, [who was ready for the challenge], accepted the assignment.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who was ready for the challenge
(b) who are ready for the challenge
(c) who was ready for the challenges
(d) who would be ready for the challenge
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause is a restrictive relative clause with past simple tense to describe a past state.
उदा. "जो चुनौतियों के लिए तैयार था…"
[RULE] Restrictive Relative Clause with Past Simple

[Q1052] The report, [which was submitted last week], is still pending approval.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which was submitted last week
(b) which is submitted last week
(c) which have been submitted last week
(d) which were submitted last week
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative clause uses past simple to indicate the action completed in the past.
उदा. "जो पिछले हफ्ते जमा किया गया था…"
[RULE] Relative Clause with Past Simple

[Q1053] He was praised for his efforts, [which resulted in increased sales].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which resulted in increased sales
(b) which results in increased sales
(c) which will result in increased sales
(d) which results in increasing sales
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative clause should use the simple past tense to show the consequence of the action.
उदा. "जिससे बिक्री बढ़ी…"
[RULE] Relative Clause with Simple Past

[Q1054] The new policy, [which has been implemented across all departments], aims to improve efficiency.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which has been implemented across all departments
(b) which had been implemented across all departments
(c) which will be implemented across all departments
(d) which is implemented across all departments
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Present perfect continuous is used to indicate an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
उदा. "जो सभी विभागों में लागू किया गया है…"
[RULE] Present Perfect Continuous in Relative Clause

[Q1055] The board members, [who had endorsed the plan], were confident about the out come
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who had endorsed the plan
(b) who has endorsed the plan
(c) who endorses the plan
(d) who will endorse the plan
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Past perfect tense is used in a relative clause to show an action completed before another past action.
उदा. "जिन्होंने योजना को स्वीकार किया था…"
[RULE] Relative Clause with Past Perfect

[Q1056] The students, [who is working hard], are expected to pass the exams.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who is working hard
(b) who are working hard
(c) who work hard
(d) who has worked hard
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The subject of the clause is 'students', a plural noun; therefore, the verb must be plural 'are'.
उदा. "जो कड़ी मेहनत कर रहे हैं…"
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement in Relative Clause

[Q1057] The project, [which is expected to be completed by August], will be reviewed next month.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which is expected to be completed by August
(b) which expected to be completed by August
(c) which has been expected to be completed by August
(d) which will be expected to be completed by August
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause requires a passive construction with the present simple to indicate a scheduled future event.
उदा. "जिसे अगस्त तक पूरा होने की उम्मीद है…"
[RULE] Passive Construction in Relative Clause

[Q1058] The manager as well as his subordinates were present at the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was present
(b) are present
(c) were being present
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject (The manager, which is singular). Hence, 'was present' is correct.
उदा. जब दो कर्ता 'as well as' से जुड़ते हैं, तो क्रिया पहले कर्ता (singular) के अनुसार आती है। इसलिए 'was' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'as well as'

[Q1059] She is more smarter than her sister in solving puzzles.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) much smarter
(b) smarter
(c) more smart
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Double comparatives ('more smarter') are grammatically incorrect. 'Smart' takes '-er' for its comparative form ('smarter').
उदा. एक साथ दो comparative words ('more' और 'smarter') का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं किया जा सकता। सही शब्द 'smarter' है।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparatives

[Q1060] Neither of the two candidates have submitted their documents on time.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has submitted his
(b) have submitted his
(c) has submitted their
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither of' takes a singular verb and singular pronoun ('his'). Hence, 'has submitted his' is correct.
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद singular verb ('has') और singular possessive pronoun ('his') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Pronoun and Verb Agreement with 'Neither of'

[Q1061] He told to me that he would help me in my crisis.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) told me
(b) said me
(c) told to I
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Tell' is a transitive verb when followed by an object, so it does not take the preposition 'to' after it. 'Told me' is correct.
उदा. 'Tell' के बाद सीधा object आता है, बीच में 'to' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है।
[RULE] Transitive Verbs (Tell vs Say)

[Q1062] If I was you, I would not accept this project.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) If I were you
(b) If I am you
(c) If I has been you
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
For hypothetical or imaginary conditional sentences, 'were' is used with all subjects, not 'was'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Hypothetical sentences) में सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'was' का नहीं।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood / Conditional Sentences

[Q1063] The furniture in his new house are quite expensive and elegant.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) is quite expensive
(b) were quite expensive
(c) are being expensive
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb ('is').
उदा. 'Furniture' एक Uncountable Noun है, जिसके साथ हमेशा Singular Verb ('is') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Uncountable Nouns and Agreement

[Q1064] Despite of working hard, he could not clear the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite working
(b) In spite working
(c) Despite of worked
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (Note: 'In spite of' takes 'of'). Therefore, 'Despite working' is correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है। ('In spite of' होता है)।
[RULE] Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

[Q1065] One of the most efficient employee has been transferred to the headquarters.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) most efficient employees have
(b) most efficient employees has
(c) more efficient employee has
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
After 'One of the', the noun must be plural ('employees'), but the verb must remain singular ('has') because the subject is 'One'.
उदा. 'One of the' के बाद Noun बहुवचन (plural) होती है ('employees'), लेकिन Verb एकवचन (singular) रहती है ('has')।
[RULE] Rule of 'One of the + Plural Noun + Singular Verb'

[Q1066] She has completed her graduation two years ago.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) completed
(b) had completed
(c) has been completing
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Words indicating past time like 'ago', 'yesterday', 'last year' require Simple Past Tense, not Present Perfect.
उदा. 'ago', 'yesterday', 'last year' जैसे शब्दों के साथ Past Indefinite Tense (V2) का प्रयोग होता है, Present Perfect का नहीं।
[RULE] Tenses with Past Time Markers

[Q1067] The manager as well as his subordinates (were present) at the inaugural ceremony.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was present
(b) were present
(c) are present
(d) have present
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('manager', which is singular). Thus, 'was' should replace 'were'.
उदा. जब दो कर्ता 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो क्रिया (verb) पहले कर्ता के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'manager' एकवचन है, अतः 'were' की जगह 'was' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'as well as'

[Q1068] No sooner did the bell ring (when the students rushed) out of their classrooms.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the students rushed
(b) when the students had rushed
(c) then the students rushed
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when' or 'then'. Hence, 'than the students rushed' is the correct replacement.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा संयोजन (conjunction) के रूप में 'than' का प्रयोग होता है, 'when' या 'then' का नहीं।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (No sooner... than)

[Q1069] Hardly had I stepped out of the house (than a heavy shower) drenched me completely.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when a heavy shower
(b) than a heavy shower
(c) then a heavy shower
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction used with 'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के बाद जोड़े के रूप में 'when' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'than' का नहीं।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Hardly... when)

[Q1070] If I (was you), I would never accept such a humiliating offer.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were you
(b) am you
(c) have been you
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary or unreal situation (subjunctive mood), 'were' is used with all subjects, regardless of person or number.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive Mood) में सभी विषयों (subjects) के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, चाहे वह एकवचन हो या बहुवचन।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood / Conditional Sentences

[Q1071] She is one of those persons who (always speaks) the truth regardless of the consequences.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) always speak
(b) always speaks
(c) is always speaking
(d) has always spoken
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In sentences starting with 'one of those + plural noun + relative pronoun (who/which)', the verb following the relative pronoun agrees with the plural antecedent (persons), so 'speak' should be used.
उदा. 'one of those + बहुवचन संज्ञा + who' की संरचना में relative pronoun (who) के बाद आने वाली क्रिया अपने antecedent (persons) के अनुसार बहुवचन (plural) होगी।
[RULE] Relative Pronoun & Subject-Verb Agreement

[Q1072] Neither the teacher nor the students (was) present in the auditorium.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were
(b) was
(c) is
(d) are
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('students', which is plural). Therefore, 'were' is correct.
उदा. जब दो कर्ता 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो क्रिया नजदीक वाले कर्ता (students) के अनुसार बहुवचन (were) होगी।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Neither... nor'

[Q1073] He is superior (than me) in both intelligence and experience.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) to me
(b) than me
(c) to mine
(d) from me
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Adjectives ending in '-ior' (such as superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior) take the preposition 'to' instead of 'than'.
उदा. जिन विशेषणों के अंत में '-ior' आता है (जैसे superior, junior आदि), उनके बाद 'than' के स्थान पर 'to' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Fixed Prepositions with Adjectives (-ior)

[Q1074] The committee (are divided) in its opinion regarding the new policy implementation.

[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) is divided
(b) are divided
(c) has divided
(d) were divide
[ANS] b
[SOL]
A collective noun like 'committee' takes a plural verb and plural pronoun when its members are divided in opinion. Here 'are divided' is correct as it refers to individual members.
उदा. जब collective noun (जैसे committee) के सदस्यों में मतभेद हो, तो उसके साथ बहुवचन (plural) क्रिया और सर्वनाम का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Collective Nouns & Verb Agreement

[Q1075] Each of the participants (were given) a certificate of appreciation at the end of the work shop

[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) was given
(b) were given
(c) have given
(d) are given
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The pronoun 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb. Hence, 'was given' must replace 'were given'.
उदा. 'Each' शब्द हमेशा एकवचन (singular) होता है और इसके साथ एकवचन क्रिया का प्रयोग होता है, अतः 'were' की जगह 'was' आएगा।
[RULE] Pronoun 'Each' with Singular Verb

(c) then the train left

[SOL]

(b) was writing
(c) had written
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Since 'for the last three years' indicates an action starting in the past and continuing into the present within a past narrative context, the past perfect continuous tense 'had been writing' or present perfect continuous is required. Wait, reporting verb is past ('told'), so present continuous 'is writing' becomes past perfect continuous 'had been writing'. Let's use 'had been writing'.
💡 हिन्दी व्याख्या: सही विकल्प 'has been writing' है। वाक्य के व्याकरणिक नियमों के अनुसार इसे शुद्ध किया गया है।
[RULE] Tense consistency and time clauses (since/for)

[Q1111] Neither of the two candidates have cleared the written examination.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) has cleared
(b) were cleared
(c) are cleared
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun/pronoun but takes a singular verb. Therefore, 'have' should be replaced by 'has'.
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद प्लूरल नाउन आता है लेकिन वर्ब हमेशा सिंगुलर होती है। अतः 'have' की जगह 'has' होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Neither of'

[Q1112] If I was the king, I would eradicate poverty from the country.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) If I am the king
(b) If I were the king
(c) If I will be the king
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary or unreal past/present situation (subjunctive mood), 'were' is used with all subjects, not 'was'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive Mood) में सभी सब्जेक्ट्स के साथ 'was' की जगह 'were' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood (Conditional Sentences)

[Q1113] The furniture in his new house look very expensive and elegant.

(a) looks very expensive
(b) are looking very expensive
(c) were looking very expensive
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb. Therefore, 'look' must be replaced by 'looks'.
उदा. 'Furniture' एक अनकाउंटेबल नाउन है और इसके साथ हमेशा सिंगुलर वर्ब आती है। अतः 'look' का 'looks' होगा।

(b) taller than her sister
(c) most tallest than her sister
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Double comparatives ('more taller') are grammatically incorrect. The correct comparative form of 'tall' is simply 'taller'.
उदा. दो कॉम्परेटिव एक साथ (more taller) प्रयोग नहीं होते। 'tall' की कॉम्परेटिव डिग्री 'taller' होती है।

'Despite' is never followed by 'of', whereas 'In spite' takes 'of'.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है ('In spite of' होता है)।
[RULE] Prepositional Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

---

[Q1154] She looks as if she **knows every thing** about the secret project.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) knows everything
(b) knew everything
(c) had known everything
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'As if' / 'As though' denoting an unreal past situation takes the past subjunctive form ('knew').
उदा. 'As if' के बाद काल्पनिक स्थिति बताने के लिए Past Tense (knew) का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Conditional / Subjunctive Sentences

---

[Q1155] The principal along with his teachers **are attending** the seminar.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) are attending
(b) is attending
(c) were attending
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When subjects are connected by 'along with', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The principal', which is singular).
उदा. जब दो subjects 'along with' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject ('principal') के अनुसार singular (is) होगी।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Along with)

---

[Q1156] Hardly had I stepped out of the house when a heavy downpour starts.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) downpour started
(b) downpour will start
(c) downpour is starting
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The sentence begins with 'Hardly had', which is in the past tense. Therefore, the second clause connected by 'when' must also be in the past tense ('started').
उदा. 'Hardly had' पास्ट टेंस में है, इसलिए 'when' के बाद वाला उपवाक्य भी पास्ट टेंस (started) में होना चाहिए।
[RULE] Correlative conjunctions (Hardly... when) and consistency of tense

---

[Q1157] Neither of the two candidates have qualified for the final interview.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) has qualified
(b) are qualified
(c) were qualified
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither of' takes a singular verb because it refers to each one individually. Thus, 'have' should be replaced by 'has'.
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद हमेशा एकवचन (singular) वर्ब का प्रयोग होता है, इसलिए 'have' की जगह 'has' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Neither of'

---

[Q1158] She is more smarter than any other student in her class.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) much smarter
(b) smarter
(c) most smarter
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Double comparatives ('more smarter') are grammatically incorrect. 'Smarter' is already the comparative form of 'smart'.
उदा. दो कम्पेरेटिव शब्दों का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं होता ('more smarter' गलत है, सही 'smarter' है)।
[RULE] Superfluous Adjectives / Comparative Degree

---

[Q1159] The manager asked me that why I was late to the office.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) asked me why I was
(b) enquired me why was I
(c) asked to me why I was
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In indirect speech, reporting verbs like 'asked' are not followed by 'that' when introducing a wh-question. Also, the clause structure becomes subject + verb.
उदा. इनडायरेक्ट स्पीच में 'asked' के बाद 'that' का प्रयोग नहीं होता और प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य साधारण वाक्य (Subject + Verb) बन जाता है।
[RULE] Direct and Indirect Speech (Interrogative Sentences)

---

[Q1160] She insisted to accompany her brother to the market.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) insisted on accompanying
(b) insisted for accompanying
(c) insisted to accompanying
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb 'insist' is always followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund (-ing form), i.e., 'insisted on accompanying'.
उदा. 'Insist' वर्ब के बाद हमेशा 'on' प्रीपोज़िशन और उसके बाद जरंड (-ing फॉर्म) का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Fixed Prepositions with Gerunds

---

[Q1161] He is superior than most of his colleagues in technical skills.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) superior to
(b) more superior than
(c) more superior to
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Adjectives ending in '-or' (such as superior, inferior, senior, junior) are followed by the preposition 'to', not 'than'.
उदा. जिन विशेषणों के अंत में '-or' आता है (जैसे superior, junior आदि), उनके बाद 'than' की जगह 'to' प्रीपोज़िशन का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Adjectives taking 'to' instead of 'than'

---

[Q1162] The project, ___, was completed on time.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which had been delayed
(b) which is delayed
(c) that was delayed
(d) that had been delayed
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Use of past perfect in a non‑defining relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘The project, which had been delayed, was completed on time.’
[RULE] Non‑defining relative clause with past perfect

[Q1163] He is the only person ___.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who can help us
(b) that can help us
(c) whom can help us
(d) was able to help us
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use of ‘who’ for people in a restrictive relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘He is the only person who can help us.’
[RULE] Restrictive relative clause – ‘who’ for people

[Q1164] The company has been looking for a candidate ___.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who can work in 6 months

(c) who could work within 6 months

[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use of ‘within’ to indicate a time limit.
उदाहरण: ‘…a candidate who can work within 6 months.’
[RULE] Time expression – ‘within’ + time duration

[Q1165] The book, ___, is on the shelf.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which I bought last week
(b) which I had bought last week
(c) Candid
(d) Dubious
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use of past perfect in a non‑defining relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘The book, which I had bought last week, is on the shelf.’
[RULE] Non‑defining relative clause with past perfect

[Q1166] The committee had appointed a member ___.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who will be the chairperson
(b) who would be the chairperson
(c) who is the chairperson
(d) who has been chairperson
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use of future simple in a relative clause to indicate a future role.
उदाहरण: ‘…a member who will be the chairperson.’
[RULE] Future simple in a relative clause

[Q1167] He promised to finish the work ___.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) by tomorrow
(b) by tomorrow's
(c) on tomorrow

[ANS] a
[SOL]
Correct preposition ‘by’ with a time expression.
उदाहरण: ‘He promised to finish the work by tomorrow.’
[RULE] Preposition ‘by’ + time expression

[Q1168] The report was sent to the manager ___.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who I had met yesterday
(b) who I met yesterday
(c) whom I met yesterday
(d) whom whom I met yesterday
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Use of ‘whom’ as object of the verb in a restrictive relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘…the manager whom I met yesterday.’
[RULE] Restrictive relative clause – ‘whom’ as object

[Q1169] It is difficult to keep the train ___.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) running on time
(b) running at time
(c) running on the time
(d) running at the time
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Correct infinitive complement: ‘running on time’.
उदाहरण: ‘It is difficult to keep the train running on time.’
[RULE] Infinitive complement – ‘running on time’

[Q1170] The manager, ___, will decide the salary.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who will decide the salary

(d) who has decided the salary
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use of future simple in a non‑defining relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘The manager, who will decide the salary, …’
[RULE] Non‑defining relative clause – future simple

[Q1171] She was praised for ___.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) her effort
(b) her efforts
(c) her effort's

[ANS] a
[SOL]
Singular noun ‘effort’ used with ‘for’ when referring to one action.
उदाहरण: ‘She was praised for her effort.’

[Q1172] The students, ___, presented the project to the panel.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who had prepared it beforehand
(b) who had prepared it before
(c) Timid
(d) Uncanny
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use of past perfect in a non‑defining relative clause.
उदाहरण: ‘The students, who had prepared it beforehand, presented the project…’

[Q1173] The manager as well as his subordinates [were present] at the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was present
(b) were present
(c) are present
(d) have present
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('manager' is singular).
उदा. जब दो Subject 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो Verb हमेशा पहले Subject के अनुसार आती है ('manager' एक वचन है, इसलिए 'was' आएगा)।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (as well as)

[Q1174] Hardly had I stepped out of the house [than it began to rain].
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when it began to rain
(b) than it began to rain
(c) then it began to rain
(d) that it began to rain
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is always followed by 'when' (not 'than').
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, 'than' का नहीं (Hardly... when)।
[RULE] Conjunction Pair (Hardly... when)

[Q1175] She [is knowing] the secret of this success for a long time.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has known
(b) is knowing
(c) knows
(d) has been knowing
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Verbs of perception/state like 'know' are not used in continuous tenses. With 'for a long time', Present Perfect Tense is used.
उदा. 'Know' एक Stative Verb है, इसे Continuous Tense में नहीं लिखते। समय (for a long time) दिया होने पर Present Perfect ('has known') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Stative Verbs / Tenses

[Q1176] Neither of the two candidates [have returned] the library books yet.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has returned
(b) have returned
(c) returned
(d) are returning
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb.
उदा. 'Neither of', 'Either of', 'Each of' के बाद Noun बहुवचन (plural) होता है लेकिन Verb हमेशा एकवचन (singular) आती है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Neither of)

[Q1177] He is [too clever] to understand this simple trick.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) so clever
(b) too clever
(c) very clever
(d) enough clever
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The structure 'too... to' conveys a negative meaning equivalent to 'so... that cannot'. The sentence is contextually and grammatically correct as is.
उदा. 'too... to' का प्रयोग नकारात्मक परिणाम के लिए होता है। यहाँ 'too clever' बिल्कुल सही है क्योंकि इसका अर्थ है वह इतना चालाक है कि ट्रिक नहीं समझ सकता।
[RULE] Too... to Structure

[Q1178] No sooner did the police arrive [than the thieves fled].
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the thieves fled
(b) when the thieves fled
(c) then the thieves fled
(d) as the thieves fled
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'No sooner' is always followed by 'than'.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का जोड़ा बनता है, जो यहाँ बिल्कुल सही दिया गया है।
[RULE] Conjunction Pair (No sooner... than)

[Q1179] If I [was you], I would never accept such humiliating conditions.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were you
(b) was you
(c) am you
(d) had been you
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In unreal conditional sentences expressing a wish or hypothetical situation, 'were' is used for all subjects.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Hypothetical sentences) में सभी Subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, चाहे Subject सिंगुलर ही क्यों न हो ('If I were you')।
[RULE] Conditional Sentences (Subjunctive Mood)

[Q1180] One of my best friends [are going] abroad for higher studies.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) is going
(b) are going
(c) were going
(d) have gone
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'One of' takes a plural noun and a singular verb.
उदा. 'One of' के बाद Noun plural होता है, लेकिन Verb हमेशा singular ('is') आती है क्योंकि मुख्य Subject 'One' होता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (One of)

[Q1181] She speaks English [so fluently that] every one is impressed.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) so fluently that
(b) too fluently that
(c) very fluently so
(d) as fluently that
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The correct correlative structure for cause and effect is 'so + adverb/adjective + that'.
उदा. परिणाम दिखाने के लिए 'so... that' का सही जोड़ा प्रयोग होता है ('so fluently that')।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (so... that)

[Q1182] The teacher asked the students [why are they making] so much noise.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) why they were making
(b) why are they making
(c) why were they making
(d) why they are making
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In indirect speech (reported questions), the order becomes Subject + Verb, not Verb + Subject. Also, past tense is required.
उदा. Indirect Speech में प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य साधारण वाक्य (Subject + Verb) बन जाता है और Tense भी Past ('were making') हो जाता है।
[RULE] Direct-Indirect Narration (Interrogative Sentences)

[Q1183] She is *more smarter than* her sister in solving mathematical puzzles.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) much smarter than
(b) more smart than
(c) smarter than
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Double comparatives are grammatically incorrect in English. 'Smarter' is already a comparative form, so adding 'more' before it is redundant.
उदा. एक साथ दो comparative words ('more' और 'smarter') का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं होता। 'Smarter' स्वयं comparative है, अतः केवल 'smarter than' सही है।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparatives

[Q1184] If I *was you*, I would never accept such a humiliating offer.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) am you
(b) were you
(c) have been you
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an unreal past or hypothetical situation (subjunctive mood), 'were' is used with all subjects, even singular ones like 'I'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Hypothetical sentences) में सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood (Conditional Sentences)

[Q1185] The manager told his subordinates that *every employee must submit their report* by Friday.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) every employee must submit his report
(b) every employee must submit its report
(c) every employee must submit our report
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Every' is a singular distributive pronoun/adjective. Therefore, it requires a singular masculine pronoun ('his') in standard traditional grammar when gender is unspecified.
उदा. 'Every' एक singular शब्द है, इसलिए इसके लिए singular pronoun 'his' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए न कि plural 'their' का।
[RULE] Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement

[Q1186] Not only the teacher *but also the students was* excited about the upcoming excursion.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) but also the students were
(b) but the students was
(c) but also the students is
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, 'students' is plural, so the verb must be 'were'.
उदा. 'Not only... but also' से जुड़े होने पर verb अपने सबसे पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'students' plural है, अतः 'were' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Correlative Conjunctions)

[Q1187] She insisted *to accompany me* to the railway station despite my refusal.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) insisted on accompanying me
(b) insisted to accompanying me
(c) insisted for accompanying me
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb 'insist' is invariably followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund (verb + ing), hence 'insisted on accompanying'.
उदा. 'Insist' के बाद हमेशा preposition 'on' और उसके बाद gerund (verb+ing) का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Fixed Prepositions & Gerunds

---

[Q1188] Scarcely had we reached the station *than the train departed*.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when the train departed
(b) then the train departed
(c) as the train departed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' must always be followed by 'when' or 'before', never by 'than' or 'then'.
उदा. 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, 'than' का नहीं।
[RULE] Conjunction Pairs (Scarcely... when)

---

[Q1189] He is one of those persons who *always speaks* the truth no matter what the consequences are.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) always speak
(b) always speaking
(c) always has spoken
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In the structure 'One of + plural noun + relative pronoun (who/which/that) + plural verb', the verb inside the relative clause must agree with the plural antecedent ('persons'). Hence, 'speak'.
उदा. 'One of + plural noun + relative pronoun' की ساخت में relative pronoun के बाद आने वाली verb plural होती है क्योंकि वह antecedent (persons) को refer करती है।
[RULE] Relative Pronouns & Verb Agreement

[Q1190] Neither of the two candidates *were selected* for the final round of the interview.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was selected
(b) have been selected
(c) are selected
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither', 'Either', 'Everyone', 'Each' are singular indefinite pronouns and take a singular verb. Therefore, 'was selected' is correct.
उदा. 'Neither' का प्रयोग singular subject के रूप में होता है, इसलिए इसके साथ singular verb 'was' आएगी न कि 'were'।
[RULE] Indefinite Pronouns & Subject-Verb Agreement

[Q1191] Despite of working hard, *he failed to secure* the desired rank in the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) Despite working hard
(b) In spite of working hardly
(c) Despite of worked hard
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (Note: 'In spite' takes 'of', but 'Despite' does not). Hence, 'Despite working hard' is correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है ('In spite of' के साथ 'of' आता है)।
[RULE] Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

[Q1192] The manager asked [the new employee] to provide the report.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) the new employee
(b) the new employees
(c) the new employee's
(d) the new employee to
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: The verb *asked* requires a direct object and an infinitive clause. The correct phrase is *the new employee*.
उदाहरण: Manager ने नए कर्मचारी से रिपोर्ट देने के लिए कहा।
[RULE] Direct Object + Infinitive

---

[Q1193] She is looking forward to [meeting the new team] in the morning.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) meeting the new team
(b) meet the new team
(c) meeting the new teams
(d) to meet the new team
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: *Looking forward to* is followed by a gerund. The phrase must be *meeting the new team*.
उदाहरण: वह सुबह नए टीम से मिलने के लिए उत्सुक है।
[RULE] Gerund after Preposition

---

[Q1194] The committee decided [to postpone the meeting] until further notice.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to postpone the meeting
(b) postponing the meeting
(c) to postponement the meeting
(d) postponed the meeting
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *decided*, the infinitive form *to postpone* is used.
उदाहरण: समिति ने बैठक को आगे के नोटिस तक स्थगित करने का निर्णय लिया।
[RULE] Infinitive after Verb *decided*

---

[Q1195] It is essential that he [arrive on time] for the interview.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) arrive on time
(b) arrives on time
(c) arriving on time
(d) to arrive on time
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *essential that*, an infinitive without *to* is used. Hence *arrive on time*.
उदाहरण: यह आवश्यक है कि वह साक्षात्कार के लिए समय पर पहुंचे।
[RULE] Subjunctive with *essential that*

---

[Q1196] The students were asked [to submit the assignment] before Friday.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to submit the assignment
(b) submit the assignment
(c) submitting the assignment
(d) submitted the assignment
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: The passive form *were asked* is followed by the infinitive *to submit*.
उदाहरण: छात्रों से शुक्रवार से पहले असाइनमेंट जमा करने के लिए कहा गया।
[RULE] Passive + Infinitive

---

[Q1197] He will be responsible for [overseeing the project] until its completion.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) overseeing the project
(b) oversee the project
(c) overseen the project
(d) to oversee the project
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: The phrase *responsible for* is followed by a gerund. So *overseeing the project* is correct.
उदाहरण: वह परियोजना के पूरा होने तक उसकी निगरानी के लिए ज़िम्मेदार होगा।
[RULE] Gerund after *responsible for*

---

[Q1198] The engineer suggested [using a new algorithm] to improve accuracy.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) using a new algorithm
(b) use a new algorithm
(c) used a new algorithm
(d) to use a new algorithm
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *suggested*, a gerund is used. Hence *using a new algorithm*.
उदाहरण: इंजीनियर ने सटीकता बढ़ाने के लिए नए एल्गोरिद्म का उपयोग करने का सुझाव दिया।
[RULE] Gerund after *suggested*

---

[Q1199] It was decided [to postpone the launch] due to technical issues.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to postpone the launch
(b) postponing the launch
(c) to postponed the launch
(d) postpone the launch
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *was decided*, the infinitive *to postpone* follows.
उदाहरण: तकनीकी समस्याओं के कारण लॉन्च को स्थगित करने का निर्णय लिया गया।
[RULE] Infinitive after *was decided*

---

[Q1200] The direct or insisted [that the project be completed] by the end of the month.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) that the project be completed
(b) that the project completed
(c) that the project is completed
(d) that completing the project
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *insisted*, a subjunctive clause starts with *that* and the verb in base form *be*.
उदाहरण: निदेशक ने परियोजना को महीने के अंत तक पूरा करने पर जोर दिया।
[RULE] Subjunctive with *insisted*

---

[Q1201] The committee is concerned about [the delay in the project] affecting the schedule.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) the delay in the project
(b) delay in the project
(c) the delayed project
(d) delay of the project
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: *Concerned about* is followed by a noun phrase. The correct phrase is *the delay in the project*.
उदाहरण: समिति परियोजना में देरी के कारण शेड्यूल पर प्रभाव पड़ने की चिंता कर रही है।
[RULE] Noun phrase after *concerned about*

---

[Q1202] The team was praised for [their hard work] during the crisis.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) their hard work
(b) their hard works
(c) their hard working
(d) Judicious
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: After *praised for*, a singular noun phrase is used. Correct is *their hard work*.
उदाहरण: टीम को संकट के दौरान उनके कठिन परिश्रम के लिए प्रशंसा मिली।
[RULE] Singular noun phrase after *praised for*

---

[Q1203] Hardly had I reached the station **than the train left**.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the train left
(b) when the train left
(c) then the train left
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Hardly/Scarcely' is always followed by 'when' or 'before', not 'than' (which is used with 'No sooner'). Hence, 'when the train left' is correct.
उदा. 'Hardly/Scarcely' के बाद हमेशा 'when' या 'before' का प्रयोग होता है, न कि 'than' का।
[RULE] Correlative conjunctions (Hardly... when)

---

[Q1204] The principal as well as the teachers **were present** in the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were present
(b) are present
(c) was present
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
When two subjects are connected by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The principal', singular). Thus, 'was present' is correct.
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'as well as' से जुड़ते हैं, तो वर्ब पहले सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'The principal' एक वचन है, इसलिए 'was' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (as well as)

---

[Q1205] Neither of the two candidates **have qualified** for the post.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) have qualified
(b) has qualified
(c) are qualified
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Neither of', 'Either of', and 'Each of' always take a singular verb because they refer to individuals separately. Hence, 'has qualified' is correct.
उदा. 'Neither of', 'Either of' और 'Each of' के बाद सिंगुलर वर्ब का प्रयोग होता है क्योंकि ये एक समय में एक की बात करते हैं।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Neither of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb)

---

[Q1206] She told me that she **has bought** a new car the previous day.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has bought
(b) had bought
(c) bought
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The reporting verb 'told' is in the past tense, and 'the previous day' indicates a past time before another past action. Therefore, past perfect tense 'had bought' should be used.
उदा. यदि रिपोर्टिंग वर्ब पास्ट टेंस में हो और वाक्य में 'the previous day' दिया हो, तो पास्ट परफेक्ट टेंस ('had + V3') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Direct-Indirect / Sequence of Tenses

---

[Q1207] No sooner did the sun rise **when the fog disappeared**.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when the fog disappeared
(b) than the fog disappeared
(c) then the fog disappeared
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'No sooner' is strictly followed by the conjunction 'than', not 'when'. Hence, 'than the fog disappeared' is correct.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'when' का नहीं।
[RULE] Correlative conjunctions (No sooner... than)

---

[Q1208] She is one of those women who **always speaks** the truth.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) always speaks
(b) always speak
(c) is always speaking
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In the structure 'One of + Plural Noun + Relative Pronoun (who/which/that) + Plural Verb', the verb must agree with the plural antecedent ('women'). Thus, 'always speak' is correct.
उदा. 'One of + Plural Noun + who' की बनावट में रिलेटिव प्रोनाउन (who) से पहले आने वाले प्लुरल नाउन के अनुसार प्लुरल वर्ब (speak) का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Relative Pronoun & Subject-Verb Agreement

---

[Q1209] He is superior **than me** in intelligence and capability.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than me
(b) to me
(c) then me
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Adjectives ending in '-or' such as superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior, etc., are followed by the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Hence, 'to me' is correct.
उदा. 'superior', 'junior', 'senior' जैसे एडजेक्टिव्स के बाद 'than' के स्थान पर हमेशा 'to' का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Fixed Prepositions with Adjectives

---

[Q1210] Despite of his hard work, **he failed** to secure good marks.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) Despite of his hard work
(b) In spite of his hard work
(c) Despite his hard work
(d) Both 2 and 3
[ANS] d
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of' (Despite = In spite of). Therefore, both 'In spite of his hard work' and 'Despite his hard work' are grammatically correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता, जबकि 'In spite' के साथ 'of' आता है। अतः विकल्प 2 और 3 दोनों सही हैं।
[RULE] Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

---

[Q1211] Each boy and each girl **were given** a prize by the direct or.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were given
(b) was given
(c) have been given
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When two singular subjects are preceded by 'Each' and connected by 'and', the verb must be singular. Hence, 'was given' is correct.
उदा. जब दो सिंगुलर नाउन 'Each' से जुड़े हों और 'and' से मिलें, तो वर्ब हमेशा सिंगुलर होती है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Each... and each...)

---

[Q1212] Each of the students participating in the science fair are given a certificate of appreciation.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) is given a certificate
(b) were given a certificate
(c) are being given certificate
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When a subject begins with 'Each of', the verb that follows must be singular because 'Each' is singular.
उदा. जब वाक्य की शुरुआत 'Each of' से हो, तो इसके बाद आने वाली वर्ब हमेशा singular (एकवचन) होती है क्योंकि 'Each' एकवचन को दर्शाता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Each of'

---

[Q1213] She is more smarter than her younger sister in solving complex puzzles.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) much smarter
(b) smarter
(c) most smart
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Double comparatives ('more smarter') are grammatically incorrect. 'Smarter' is already a comparative adjective.
उदा. एक साथ दो comparative degree (more और smarter) का प्रयोग करना गलत है। 'Smarter' अपने आप में comparative है।
[RULE] Superfluous use of Double Comparatives

---

[Q1214] No sooner did the bell ring when the students rushed out of their classrooms.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the students rushed
(b) then the students rushed
(c) that the students rushed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'No sooner' must always be followed by 'than' in the correlative pair.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का जोड़ा बनता है, न कि 'when' का।
[RULE] Correlative conjunctions (No sooner... than)

---

[Q1215] Despite of working hard, he failed to secure good marks in the examination.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite working hard
(b) In spite of worked hard
(c) Although working hard
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. 'In spite of' is correct, whereas 'Despite' is used alone.
उदा. 'Despite' के बाद कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है। 'In spite of' होता है, लेकिन 'Despite' अकेला आता है।
[RULE] Preposition usage with Despite / In spite of

---

[Q1216] One of my friends are going to relocate to London next month.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) is going to relocate
(b) were going to relocate
(c) have going to relocate
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The structure 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb because the main subject is 'One'.
उदा. 'One of + plural noun' की संरचना में मुख्य subject 'One' होता है, इसलिए verb हमेशा singular (is) आती है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (One of + plural noun)

---

[Q1217] Neither the manager nor his subordinates was present at the crucial meeting.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) were present at
(b) are present at
(c) have present at
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it ('subordinates' is plural).
उदा. जब दो subject 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो verb अपने सबसे पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है ('subordinates' plural है, अतः 'were' आएगा)।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Neither... nor)

---

[Q1218] She insisted to accompany me to the railway station despite my refusal.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) insisted on accompanying
(b) insisted for accompany
(c) insisted to accompanying
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb 'insist' is always followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund (verb+ing).
उदा. 'Insist' वर्ब के बाद हमेशा preposition 'on' और उसके बाद gerund (v1+ing) का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Fixed Preposition with Gerund (Insist on)

---

[Q1219] The committee ____ the proposal after reviewing it.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has deliberated
(b) will deliberate
(c) deliberated
(d) deliberating
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Present perfect tense is used to describe an action that was completed before another past event. 
उदाहरण: "उसने रिपोर्ट लिखी है" (He has written the report).
[RULE] Present Perfect Tense

---

[Q1220] She has been studying for two hours and ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) felt tired
(b) feeling tired
(c) feels tired
(d) feelingly tired
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: Present participle is used after continuous verbs to describe an ongoing state. 
उदाहरण: "वह पढ़ रही है, इसलिए वह थकी हुई है" (She is studying, so she is feeling tired).
[RULE] Continuous Tense + Present Participle

---

[Q1221] It is ____ to accept the terms if you are not satisfied.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) reasonable
(b) reasonably
(c) reasonability
(d) reasonably's
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: An adjective is used to describe a noun, while an adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. 
उदाहरण: "यह निर्णय समझदारीपूर्ण है" (This decision is reasonable).
[RULE] Adjective vs Adverb

---

[Q1222] The new policy will be implemented after ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) the necessary approvals are obtained
(b) the necessary approvals have been obtained
(c) the necessary approvals have obtained
(d) the necessary approvals was obtained
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: The passive voice with present perfect is used when the action has been completed before a future event. 
उदाहरण: "मंजूरी मिलने के बाद ही परियोजना शुरू होगी" (The project will start after the approvals have been obtained).
[RULE] Passive Voice – Present Perfect

---

[Q1223] He gave me a book, and ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) I was grateful
(b) I am grateful
(c) I have grateful
(d) I have been grateful
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Past simple is used after a past event to describe a past feeling. 
उदाहरण: "मैंने किताब ली, और मैं आभारी था" (I received the book, and I was grateful).
[RULE] Past Simple Tense

---

[Q1224] The manager asked the team to finish the project, but they ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) did not finish
(b) didn't finish
(c) didn't finished
(d) did not finished
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: The past simple form of the verb is used after negative contractions in past tense. 
उदाहरण: "उन्हें काम पूरा नहीं किया" (They did not finish the work).
[RULE] Past Simple Tense – Negative

---

[Q1225] The students were given a chance to win a prize, however they ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) did not participate
(b) didn't participated
(c) did not participated
(d) didn't participate
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Use the past simple form after negative contraction. 
उदाहरण: "उन्हें मौका मिला, लेकिन उन्होंने भाग नहीं लिया" (They were given a chance, but they did not participate).
[RULE] Past Simple Tense – Negative

---

[Q1226] By the end of the year, the company will have ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) reached its target
(b) reaches its target
(c) reaching its target
(d) reached its targets
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Future perfect tense is used for actions that will be completed before a future time. 
उदाहरण: "वर्ष के अंत तक कंपनी अपना लक्ष्य हासिल कर लेगी" (By the end of the year, the company will have reached its target).
[RULE] Future Perfect Tense

---

[Q1227] The book was written by a famous author, and it ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has been acclaimed
(b) has acclaimed
(c) has acclaiming
(d) has acclaimeded
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Present perfect passive is used to show that an action has been completed and its effect continues. 
उदाहरण: "पुस्तक को आलोचक ने सराहा" (The book has been acclaimed).
[RULE] Present Perfect Passive

---

[Q1228] We have to finish the work before the dead line otherwise ____.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) we will be late
(b) we would be late
(c) we will be lateness
(d) we will be laten
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Future simple is used after a conditional clause to express a consequence. 
उदाहरण: "समय पर नहीं हो पाया, तो देर हो जाएगी" (Otherwise we will be late).
[RULE] Future Simple Tense – Conditional

---

[Q1229] The committee [has been discussing] the proposal for weeks.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has discussed
(b) are discussing
(c) has been discussing
(d) discussing
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The action is completed; use simple perfect tense. 
उदाहरण: समिति ने प्रस्ताव पर चर्चा कर ली है।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

---

[Q1230] She [has been studying] French since she was a child.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) studied
(b) has studied
(c) has been studying
(d) studies
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use present perfect to indicate an action that started in the past and continues. 
उदाहरण: उसने फ्रेंच का अध्ययन किया है।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

---

[Q1231] The manager [has been recommending] the new policy to the staff.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) recommended
(b) recommends
(c) has been recommending
(d) Lethargic
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The recommendation is a completed action; simple perfect is appropriate. 
उदाहरण: प्रबंधक ने नई नीति की सिफारिश की है।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

---

[Q1232] Students [are expected] to submit their assignments by Friday.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) expected
(b) are expected
(c) expected to
(d) Skeptical
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The passive form without auxiliary is sufficient. 
उदाहरण: छात्रों को शुक्रवार तक असाइनमेंट जमा करने की अपेक्षा है।
[RULE] Passive Construction

---

[Q1233] The project [has been completed] last month.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was completed
(b) has completed
(c) was completed last month
(d) has been completed last month
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Past perfect is unnecessary; simple past is correct. 
उदाहरण: परियोजना पिछले महीने पूरी हुई।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

---

[Q1234] The report [has been prepared] by the auditor.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) prepared
(b) has prepared
(c) was prepared
(d) prepared by
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The simple past passive form is sufficient. 
उदाहरण: रिपोर्ट ऑडिटर द्वारा तैयार की गई है।
[RULE] Passive Construction

[SOL]

[Q1237] The committee [has been voting] on the matter for hours.

(d) Venerable
[ANS] a
[SOL]

[Q1238] The team [has been working] on the task for days.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2022 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has worked
(b) has worked on
(c) has been working
(d) worked
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Simple perfect indicates continuous effort; no need for continuous form.

[Q1239] The manager as well as his assistants **have been arrested** for financial irregularities.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has been arrested
(b) are being arrested
(c) were arrested
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The manager', which is singular). Hence, 'has been arrested' is correct.
उदा. जब दो कर्ता 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो क्रिया (verb) पहले कर्ता के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'The manager' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'has been arrested' होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (as well as)

[Q1240] Hardly had I opened the front door **than a dog entered** the house.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when a dog entered
(b) than a dog enters
(c) then a dog entered
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is 'when' (not 'than'). Hence, 'when a dog entered' is correct.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, न कि 'than' का। इसलिए 'when a dog entered' सही विकल्प है।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Hardly... when)

[Q1241] Neither of the two candidates **have qualified** for the interview.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) has qualified
(b) are qualified
(c) were qualified
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb. Since 'candidates' is plural, the verb must be singular ('has qualified').
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद बहुवचन संज्ञा (plural noun) और एकवचन क्रिया (singular verb) का प्रयोग होता है। इसलिए 'has qualified' सही है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Neither of)

[Q1242] She is living in this city **since five years**.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) for five years
(b) from five years
(c) before five years
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
For a period of time (duration), we use 'for', not 'since'. 'Since' is used for a point of time. Thus, 'for five years' is correct.
उदा. समय की अवधि (duration) के लिए 'for' का प्रयोग किया जाता है न कि 'since' का। 'since' का प्रयोग निश्चित समय (point of time) के लिए होता है।
[RULE] Prepositions of Time (Since vs For)

[Q1243] The student apologized to the teacher **for arrive late** to the class.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) for arriving late
(b) to arrive late
(c) for arrived late
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Prepositions (like 'for') are followed by a gerund (V1+ing). Therefore, 'for arriving late' is grammatically correct.
उदा. प्रीपोज़िशन (जैसे 'for') के बाद हमेशा जेरंड (V1+ing) का प्रयोग होता है। अतः 'for arriving late' सही होगा।
[RULE] Gerunds after Prepositions

[Q1244] If I **was you**, I would not tolerate such insult.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were you
(b) am you
(c) had been you
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary situation or wish, 'were' is used with all subjects (plural and singular). Hence, 'were you' is correct.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Conditional sentences) में सभी विषयों के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है। इसलिए 'were you' सही है।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood / Conditionals

[Q1245] No sooner did the train arrive at the station **than the passengers rushed** towards it.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) no improvement
(b) when the passengers rushed
(c) then the passengers rushed
(d) as the passengers rushed
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'No sooner' is correctly followed by 'than'. The sentence is grammatically correct as written.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' का सही प्रयोग किया गया है। वाक्य में कोई सुधार की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (No sooner... than)

[Q1246] Despite of his hard work, **he could not pass** the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite his hard work
(b) In spite of his hard work,
(c) Although his hard work
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (In spite + of = Despite). Therefore, 'Despite his hard work' is correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है (In spite of = Despite)। अतः 'Despite his hard work' सही विकल्प है।
[RULE] Prepositions (Despite vs In spite of)

[Q1247] One of my friends **are going to Mumbai** next week.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) is going to Mumbai
(b) are going for Mumbai
(c) is going for Mumbai
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The structure 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb. Here, the subject is 'One', so the singular verb 'is going' must be used.
उदा. संरचना 'One of + plural noun' के साथ एकवचन क्रिया (singular verb) का प्रयोग होता है। यहाँ मुख्य कर्ता 'One' है, इसलिए 'is going' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (One of)

[Q1248] He told me that he **has bought a new car** the previous day.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) had bought a new car
(b) bought a new car
(c) has been buying a new car
(d) no improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In indirect speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense ('told'), the simple past or present perfect in direct speech changes to the past perfect tense ('had bought').
उदा. इनडायरेक्ट स्पीच में जब रिपोर्टिंग वर्ब भूतकाल (past tense) में हो, तो 'the previous day' वाले वाक्य में Past Perfect tense ('had bought') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Direct and Indirect Speech (Tense Change)

(d) No improvement

[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly/Scarcely' is 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. Therefore, the original sentence is grammatically correct.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' या 'before' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'than' का नहीं। अतः वाक्य में कोई सुधार की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Hardly... when)

(a) have paid

(d) were paid

'Neither of' is always followed by a singular verb because it refers to none of the two items individually.

[Q1251] If I was the king, I *would help* the poor and the needy.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) would help
(b) were help
(c) will help
(d) have helped

In unreal conditional sentences (subjunctive mood expressing a hypothetical wish), 'were' is used with all subjects, and the main clause takes 'would + V1'. The underlined part 'would help' is already correct.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive mood) में सभी subjects के साथ 'were' आता है और मुख्य क्लॉज में 'would + V1' का प्रयोग होता है। अतः 'would help' सही है।

[Q1252] The manager asked the employee *why did he come* late to the office.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) why did he come
(b) why he came
(c) why had he come
(d) why did he came
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In indirect speech or embedded questions, the structure changes from interrogative (wh-word + auxiliary + subject) to assertive (wh-word + subject + verb).
उदा. Indirect speech या embedded question में प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य साधारण वाक्य (subject + verb) बन जाता है। इसलिए 'why he came' सही होगा।
[RULE] Indirect Speech / Embedded Questions

[Q1253] He is one of those persons who *is always ready* to help others.

(c) were always ready
(d) was always ready
[ANS] b

In the structure 'One of + plural noun + relative pronoun (who/which/that) + verb', the verb agrees with the plural antecedent (persons), not 'one'. Thus, 'are' is correct.
उदा. 'One of + plural noun + relative pronoun' के बाद आने वाली verb अपने antecedent (plural noun) के अनुसार plural होती है। अतः 'is' की जगह 'are' होगा।

[Q1273] Not only he cheated his friends, but he also deceived his family.

(a) No improvement

(c) He not only cheated
(d) Not only he cheats

For parallel construction with 'not only... but also', 'not only' should be placed immediately before the word it modifies, or inversion can be used on the first clause ('Not only did he cheat'). Here, placing it after the subject ('He not only cheated') makes it parallel with 'he also deceived'.
उदा. 'Not only... but also' में parallelism का नियम लगता है। 'He not only cheated... but he also deceived' सबसे सही और सरल सुधार है।

(a) No improvement
(b) Despite working hard
(c) In spite of worked hard
(d) Although working hard

[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. 'In spite' takes 'of', but 'Despite' stands alone.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है ('In spite of' होता है)। अतः सही विकल्प 'Despite working hard' है।
[RULE] Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

---

[Q1275] The committee are divided in their opinion regarding the new policy.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) No improvement
(b) is divided in its
(c) are divided in its
(d) is divided in their
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When a collective noun like 'committee' shows division among its members, it takes a plural verb and plural pronoun ('their'). The sentence is grammatically correct.
उदा. जब collective noun ('committee') में मतभेद हो, तो वह plural verb ('are') और plural pronoun ('their') लेता है। वाक्य बिल्कुल सही है।
[RULE] Collective Nouns and Division of Opinion

---

[Q1276] One of my friends are a renowned scientist working in NASA.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) No improvement
(b) is a renowned scientist
(c) are renowned scientists
(d) is a renowned scientists
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'One of' is followed by a plural noun ('friends') but takes a singular verb ('is') because the subject is 'One'.
उदा. 'One of' के बाद plural noun आता है लेकिन verb हमेशा singular ('is') होती है क्योंकि मुख्य subject 'One' होता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'One of + Plural Noun'

---

[Q1277] Each of the students participating in the drawing competition <span class under line have been given< / span> a box of crayons.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) have been given
(b) has been given
(c) were given
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Each of' is followed by a plural noun/pronoun but the verb must always be singular because the subject is 'Each'.
उदा. 'Each of' के बाद plural noun आता है, लेकिन verb हमेशा singular (has) होती है क्योंकि मुख्य subject 'Each' है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Each of'

---

[Q1278] She is <span class under line more smarter< / span> than her sister in solving puzzles.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) more smarter
(b) much smarter
(c) smarter
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Double comparatives ('more smarter') are grammatically incorrect. 'Smarter' is already the comparative form of 'smart'.
उदा. दो comparative degrees का एक साथ प्रयोग गलत होता है। 'smart' की comparative form 'smarter' होती है, इसलिए 'more' अनावश्यक है।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparatives

---

[Q1279] If I <span class under line was the king< / span>, I would eradicate poverty from the country.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was the king
(b) were the king
(c) am the king
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary situation or unreal past desire, 'were' is used with all subjects, not 'was'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive mood) में सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।
[RULE] Conditional Sentences (Subjunctive Mood)

---

[Q1280] The manager asked the employee why he <span class under line'>is coming< / span> late to the office every day.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) is coming
(b) was coming
(c) comes
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The reporting verb ('asked') is in the past tense, and 'every day' denotes a habitual action. Therefore, the simple present tense ('comes') should be used in indirect speech for universal/habitual truths.
उदा. Reporting verb past tense में है और 'every day' आदत (habit) को दर्शाता है, इसलिए यहाँ simple present tense (comes) का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Direct-Indirect Speech & Tense Consistency

[Q1281] No sooner did the train stop at the platform <span class under line than the passengers rushed< / span> towards the compartments.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the passengers rushed
(b) when the passengers rushed
(c) then the passengers rushed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'No sooner' is always followed by 'than', not 'when' or 'then'. The structure used here is correct.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'when' या 'then' का नहीं। वाक्य में दी गई संरचना पूर्णतः सही है।
[RULE] Conjunctional Pairs (No sooner... than)

---

[Q1282] He is one of those persons who <span class under line does not tolerate< / span> nonsense.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) does not tolerate
(b) do not tolerate
(c) did not tolerated
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In the phrase 'one of those + plural noun + relative pronoun (who) + plural verb', the verb must agree with the antecedent ('persons'), which is plural. Hence, 'do not tolerate' is correct.
उदा. 'One of those + plural noun + who' की संरचना में verb अपने antecedent (persons) के अनुसार plural (do not tolerate) होती है।
[RULE] Relative Pronoun & Verb Agreement

---

[Q1283] The scientist <span class under line has invented< / span> a new vaccine last year.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has invented
(b) invented
(c) had invented
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Adverbs of past time like 'last year', 'yesterday', 'ago' require the Simple Past Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.
उदा. 'last year' जैसे past time indicators के साथ Simple Past Tense (invented) का प्रयोग होता है, Present Perfect का नहीं।
[RULE] Simple Past Tense with Past Time Markers

---

[Q1284] Neither the teacher nor the students <span class under line was present< / span> at the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was present
(b) were present
(c) is present
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, the closest subject is 'students' (plural), so 'were present' is correct.
उदा. जब दो subjects 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो verb अपने सबसे पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'students' plural है, अतः 'were' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Neither... nor'

[Q1285] The book was read by the teacher, ______ the class was excited.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) and
(b) so
(c) because
(d) while
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use a coordinating conjunction to join two independent clauses. The correct choice is "and".
उदाहरण: पुस्तक को शिक्षक ने पढ़ा, और कक्षा उत्साहित थी।
[RULE] Coordinating Conjunction – AND

---

[Q1286] She studied hard, ______ she passed the exam with flying colors.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) so
(b) and
(c) although
(d) because
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use "so" to indicate result. The correct choice is "so".
उदाहरण: उसने कड़ी मेहनत की, इसलिए उसने परीक्षा में शानदार अंक प्राप्त किए।
[RULE] Resultative Conjunction – SO
