[Q1287] He will come to the party, ______ he is busy with work.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) although
(b) unless
(c) and
(d) since
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause expresses contrast; "although" is appropriate.
उदाहरण: वह पार्टी में आएगा, हालांकि वह काम में व्यस्त है।
[RULE] Concessive Conjunction – ALTHOUGH

---

[Q1288] The manager advised the team to work efficiently, ______ the project dead line was tight.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) because
(b) so that
(c) although
(d) but
[ANS] b
[SOL]
"So that" shows purpose, fitting the sentence context.
उदाहरण: प्रबंधक ने टीम को कुशलतापूर्वक काम करने के लिए कहा, ताकि परियोजना की समय सीमा सख्त थी।
[RULE] Purpose Conjunction – SO THAT

---

[Q1289] He will not attend the meeting, ______ he has an important present at i on tomorrow.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) unless
(b) since
(c) although
(d) but
[ANS] a
[SOL]
"Unless" introduces a condition preventing attendance.
उदाहरण: वह बैठक में नहीं आएगा, जब तक कि उसके पास कल एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रस्तुति है।
[RULE] Conditional Conjunction – UNLESS

[Q1290] She likes to travel, ______ she never visits the same place twice.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) and
(b) so that
(c) but
(d) although

[SOL]
"But" introduces a contrast between preferences.
उदाहरण: उसे यात्रा करना पसंद है, लेकिन वह कभी भी एक ही जगह पर नहीं जाता।
[RULE] Contrastive Conjunction – BUT

[Q1291] They decided to postpone the event, ______ the weather forecast predicted rain.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) since
(b) and
(c) although
(d) because

Use "because" to give reason.
उदाहरण: उन्होंने कार्यक्रम को टालने का निर्णय लिया, क्योंकि मौसम पूर्वानुमान ने बारिश की भविष्यवाणी की।
[RULE] Causal Conjunction – BECAUSE

[Q1292] The students were diligent, ______ the exam results were outstanding.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) and
(b) so
(c) while
(d) although
[ANS] b
[SOL]
"So" indicates result.
उदाहरण: छात्र परिश्रमी थे, इसलिए परीक्षा के परिणाम उत्कृष्ट थे।
[RULE] Result Conjunction – SO

[Q1293] He will be late, ______ he forgot his keys at home.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]

(a) although
(b) because
(c) but
(d) since
[ANS] b

"Because" provides the reason for being late.
उदाहरण: वह देर से आएगा, क्योंकि उसने अपनी चाबियाँ घर पर रख दी थीं।
[RULE] Causal Conjunction – BECAUSE

[Q1294] She will join the committee, ______ she has the required experience.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2020]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) since
(b) although
(c) but
(d) because
[ANS] a
[SOL]
"Since" indicates reason and is acceptable here.
उदाहरण: वह समिति में शामिल होगी, क्योंकि उसके पास आवश्यक अनुभव है।

[Q1295] The students were encouraged ___ their essays.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to write
(b) in writing
(c) to have written
(d) for writing
[ANS] a

Verbs like *encourage* are followed by an infinitive form. Hence, *to write* is the correct choice.
उदाहरण: छात्रों को निबंध लिखने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया गया।

[Q1296] The committee requested ___ the proposal before the next meeting.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to review
(b) reviewing
(c) review
(d) reviewed
[ANS] c
[SOL]
After *request* we use a bare infinitive (verb without *to*) when expressing an action to be done. Hence, *review*.
उदाहरण: समिति ने अगले बैठक से पहले प्रस्ताव की समीक्षा करने का अनुरोध किया।

[Q1297] He is eager ___ the new job.

(a) to start
(b) starting
(c) started
(d) start
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Adjectives like *eager* are followed by an infinitive. Therefore, *to start* is correct.
उदाहरण: वह नई नौकरी शुरू करने के लिए उत्सुक है।

[Q1298] The teacher asked the students ___ the assignment by Friday.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to submit
(b) submit
(c) submitting
(d) submitted

*Ask* is followed by an infinitive. Hence, *to submit*.
उदाहरण: शिक्षक ने छात्रों से अनुरोध किया कि वे शुक्रवार तक असाइनमेंट जमा करें।
[RULE] Verb + infinitive

[Q1299] She advised her friend ___ the doctor’s appointment.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to keep
(b) keeping
(c) kept
(d) keeps
[ANS] a
[SOL]
*Advise* is followed by an infinitive. Hence, *to keep*.
उदाहरण: उसने अपनी दोस्त को डॉक्टर की अपॉइंटमेंट रखने की सलाह दी।
[RULE] Verb + infinitive

[Q1300] The manager wants the team ___ the dead line
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2024]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to meet
(b) meeting
(c) met
(d) meets
[ANS] a
[SOL]
*Want* is followed by an infinitive when expressing desire. So, *to meet*.
उदाहरण: प्रबंधक चाहता है कि टीम समय सीमा पूरी करे।
[RULE] Verb + infinitive

[Q1301] The company expects ___ new products this year.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to launch
(b) launching
(c) launched
(d) launch
[ANS] d
[SOL]
*Expect* is followed by a bare infinitive. Hence, *launch*.
उदाहरण: कंपनी इस वर्ष नए उत्पाद लॉन्च करने की उम्मीद करती है।
[RULE] Verb + bare infinitive

[Q1302] He is known ___ excellent problem‑solving skills.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) for having
(b) to have
(c) having
(d) has

[SOL]

[Q1303] The report was prepared ___ the latest data.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) using
(b) to use
(c) used
(d) use

*Prepared* is a passive verb that takes a gerund to indicate the means. Hence, *using*.

[Q1304] They agreed ___ a new project together.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to start
(b) starting
(c) started
(d) start
[ANS] a
[SOL]
*Agree* is followed by an infinitive when expressing consent. Thus, *to start*.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) will be published

(a) starts

[RULE] Subjunctive mood / base form after 'that'

(a) complete the project

(a) includes

(a) won

[Q1310] The manager warned that the project ____ if the funding is not secured.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) fails

[Q1311] She is known for ____ her students in every way possible.

[Q1312] The committee decided that the new policy ____ implemented immediately.

[Q1314] The children liked the game ____ more than the others.

[Q1315] The manager as well as his clerks <ins>were present< / ins> at the meeting.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were present
(b) was present
(c) are present
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b

When subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject (The manager, which is singular). Hence, 'was present' is correct.
उदा. जब दो subjects 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject के अनुसार आती है। 'The manager' singular है, इसलिए 'was' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'as well as'

[Q1316] Hardly had I arrived at the station <ins>than the train left< / ins>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) than the train left
(b) when the train left
(c) then the train left
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is always followed by 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. Therefore, 'when the train left' is correct.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, 'than' का नहीं (जो कि 'No sooner' के साथ आता है)।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Hardly... when)

[Q1317] Neither of the two candidates <ins>have paid< / ins> the subscription fee.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) have paid
(b) has paid
(c) are paid
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun/pronoun but takes a singular verb. Thus, 'has paid' is correct.
उदा. 'Neither of' के बाद plural noun आता है लेकिन verb हमेशा singular (has) होती है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Neither of'

[Q1318] She is one of those women who <ins>always praises< / ins> her children.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) always praises
(b) always praise
(c) is always praising
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In the structure 'one of + plural noun + relative pronoun (who) + plural verb', the verb must agree with the antecedent ('women'), which is plural. So, 'always praise' is correct.
उदा. 'one of + plural noun + who' की बनावट में relative pronoun (who) अपने से पहले आने वाले plural noun (women) को refer करता है, इसलिए verb भी plural ('praise') होगी।
[RULE] Relative Pronoun & Verb Agreement

[Q1319] If I <ins>was a bird< / ins>, I would fly across the ocean.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) was a bird
(b) were a bird
(c) am a bird
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary, unreal past or present wish, 'were' is used for all subjects. Hence, 'were a bird' is correct.
उदा. काल्पनिक इच्छा (Hypothetical condition) व्यक्त करने के लिए सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, न कि 'was' का।
[RULE] Conditional Sentences (Subjunctive Mood)

[Q1320] The weather is much more nicer today <ins>than it was yesterday< / ins>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) than it was yesterday
(b) then it was yesterday
(c) then it is yesterday
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Double comparatives like 'much more nicer' are grammatically incorrect because 'nicer' is already a comparative adjective. The original phrase 'than it was yesterday' correctly uses 'than' for comparison.
उदा. 'much more nicer' गलत है क्योंकि 'nicer' के साथ 'more' नहीं आ सकता। 'than it was yesterday' बिल्कुल सही है।
[RULE] Superfluous Adjectives / Comparative Degree

[Q1321] No sooner did the teacher enter the class room <ins>then the students stood up< / ins>.

(a) then the students stood up
(b) when the students stood up
(c) than the students stood up
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
'No sooner' is always followed by 'than', not 'then' or 'when'. Therefore, 'than the students stood up' is the correct replacement.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा संयोजन (conjunction) के रूप में 'than' का प्रयोग होता है।

[Q1322] He insisted <ins>to go< / ins> to the party despite his illness.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to go
(b) on going
(c) in going
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The verb 'insist' is strictly followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund (-ing form), i.e., 'insisted on going'.
उदा. 'Insist' verb के बाद हमेशा preposition 'on' और उसके बाद gerund (-ing form) का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

[Q1323] Each boy and each girl <ins>were given< / ins> a prize at the annual function.

(b) was given
(c) have given
(d) No improvement

[SOL]
When two singular nouns are joined by 'and' and preceded by 'each', the verb must be singular. Hence, 'was given' is correct.
उदा. जब दो singular nouns 'and' से जुड़े हों और उनके पहले 'each' का प्रयोग हो, तो verb हमेशा singular ('was') होती है।

Wait, options provided: 'doing this work' implies 'capable of doing' if 'to' is removed, but let's correct the option context). Let's adjust options: 'capable of doing this work'. [Q1345] He <u>was decided to go< / u> to the party.

[ANS] b
[SOL]
The subject *they* is plural; therefore the auxiliary should be *have*. The correct phrase is *have been working on*.

Rule: *have* + been + present participle for plural subjects.

हिंदी: बहुवचन विषय के लिए *have* प्रयोग होता है, इसलिए *have been working on* सही है।
[RULE] Present perfect continuous (plural subject)

[Q1356] In the sentence: "The committee decided to postpone the meeting till next week.", the word *till* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) until
(b) by
(c) for
(d) to
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The preposition *till* is informal; the formal and grammatically correct preposition in this context is *until*.
उदाहरण: The committee decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
[RULE] Preposition usage – *until* is the standard form for expressing a future point in time.

---

[Q1357] In the sentence: "The researcher insisted that the data was reliable.", the word *was* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were
(b) is
(c) have been
(d) were to be
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When the subject of the embedded clause is plural (*data*), the verb should be plural; hence *were* is correct.
उदाहरण: The researcher insisted that the data were reliable.
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement in subordinate clauses – plural subject requires plural verb.

[Q1358] In the sentence: "The team has been working on the project for a long time.", the word *has* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has been
(b) had
(c) have
(d) has had
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The present perfect continuous tense requires *has been* for a singular third‑person subject.
उदाहरण: The team has been working on the project for a long time.
[RULE] Tense formation – use *has been* for present perfect continuous with singular third person.

---

[Q1359] In the sentence: "The book, which was given to me by my friend, has a beautiful cover.", the phrase *was given* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was gifted
(b) has given
(c) was giving
(d) is given
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The passive form *was gifted* is more idiomatic and concise.
उदाहरण: The book, which was gifted to me by my friend, has a beautiful cover.
[RULE] Passive voice – *was gifted* is the preferred passive construction.

---

[Q1360] In the sentence: "The manager, whose proposal was accepted, has been promoted.", the phrase *was accepted* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was adopted
(b) has been adopted
(c) was adopting
(d) was adopted by
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The simple past passive *was adopted* correctly conveys that the proposal was accepted.
उदाहरण: The manager, whose proposal was adopted, has been promoted.
[RULE] Passive voice – use *was adopted* for past passive.

---

[Q1361] In the sentence: "He has been attending the workshops, which has improved his skills.", the phrase *has improved* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has improved
(b) improved
(c) has improved him
(d) improving
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The relative clause refers to a past result of the workshops, so simple past *improved* is correct.
उदाहरण: He has been attending the workshops, which improved his skills.
[RULE] Tense consistency in relative clauses – use simple past for past results.

[Q1362] In the sentence: "The committee's decision, which was announced yesterday, will be implemented soon.", the phrase *will be implemented* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) will be implemented
(b) will implement
(c) is implemented
(d) was implemented
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The sentence refers to a future action concerning the decision; the correct form is the simple present *is implemented* as a factual statement.
उदाहरण: The committee's decision, which was announced yesterday, is implemented soon.
[RULE] Future vs. present tense in factual statements – use simple present for scheduled actions.

[Q1363] In the sentence: "She promised that she would visit us after she finished her work.", the phrase *after she finished* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) after she finishes
(b) after she finished
(c) after she will finish
(d) after she has finished
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The correct future perfect construction is *after she has finished*.
उदाहरण: She promised that she would visit us after she has finished her work.
[RULE] Future perfect tense – use *has finished* to indicate completion before another future action.

[Q1364] In the sentence: "The students, who were studying in the library, were noisy.", the phrase *were noisy* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) were noisy
(b) were no longer noisy
(c) Judicious
(d) Kinetic
[ANS] b
[SOL]
To indicate that the noise has ceased, the correct phrase is *were no longer noisy*.
उदाहरण: The students, who were studying in the library, were no longer noisy.
[RULE] Negative adverbial phrase *no longer* to indicate cessation of an action.

[Q1365] In the sentence: "The project, which had been delayed, was finally completed.", the phrase *was finally completed* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was finally completing
(b) was finally completed
(c) has finally completed
(d) Quaint
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The correct tense for a completed action that follows a delay is the present perfect *has finally completed*.
उदाहरण: The project, which had been delayed, has finally completed.
[RULE] Present perfect for recent completed actions.

[Q1366] In the sentence: "He was told that he should submit the report by Friday.", the phrase *should submit* should be replaced with which of the following?
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2019]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) should submit
(b) must submit
(c) must have submitted
(d) has to submit
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The correct modal form for a requirement in the past is *has to submit*.
उदाहरण: He was told that he has to submit the report by Friday.
[RULE] Modal verb usage – *has to* for obligations in past contexts.

[Q1367] She is more taller than her sister who is studying in college.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) more tall than
(b) taller than
(c) most tall than
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Double comparatives are incorrect in English. 'Taller' is already a comparative adjective, so using 'more' before it is redundant.
उदा. एक ही विशेषण के साथ दो तुलनात्मक शब्दों ('more' और 'taller') का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं होता। केवल 'taller than' सही है।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparatives

---

[Q1368] If I was you, I would not accept this job offer.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) If I were you
(b) If I am you
(c) If I will be you
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary situation or wish, 'were' is used with all subjects, regardless of person or number. Thus, 'If I were you' is correct.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Imaginative sentences) में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood (Conditional Sentences)

[Q1369] One of the most important problem facing our country is unemployment.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) most important problems facing
(b) more important problems faced
(c) most important problem faced
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase 'One of the' is always followed by a plural noun. Therefore, 'problem' must be changed to 'problems'.
उदा. 'One of the' के बाद हमेशा बहुवचन संज्ञा (Plural Noun) का प्रयोग किया जाता है, इसलिए 'problem' की जगह 'problems' होगा।
[RULE] Noun after 'One of the'

[Q1370] No sooner did the police arrive the thief escaped.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) No sooner did the police arrive than the thief escaped
(b) No sooner the police arrived than the thief escaped
(c) No sooner did the police arrived when the thief escaped
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'No sooner' is followed by inversion (auxiliary verb before subject) and is paired with 'than'. Therefore, 'than' must be inserted before the second clause.
उदा. 'No sooner' के तुरंत बाद हेल्पिंग वर्ब आती है और इसके साथ 'than' का जोड़ा होता है।
[RULE] Inversion and Conjunction with No sooner

[Q1371] He told me that he is preparing for the competitive exams for two years.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) he was preparing for
(b) he has been preparing for
(c) he had been preparing for
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
When the reporting verb is in the past tense ('told'), the reported speech changes to the corresponding past tense. With 'for two years' indicating duration in the past, Past Perfect Continuous ('had been preparing') is required.
उदा. जब मुख्य clause भूतकाल में हो, तो आगे का वाक्य भी भूतकाल में बदलता है। 'for two years' के कारण 'had been preparing' सही होगा।
[RULE] Sequence of Tenses / Direct-Indirect Speech Conversion

[Q1372] Despite of his hard work, he could not clear the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite of working hard
(b) Despite his hard work
(c) In spite of his hardly work
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by the preposition 'of'. (Note: 'In spite' is followed by 'of'). Hence, 'Despite his hard work' is grammatically correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के बाद कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है ('In spite' के साथ 'of' आता है)।
[RULE] Prepositional Usage: Despite vs In spite of

[Q1373] Each of the participants were given a certificate of participation.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) was given a certificate
(b) were given certificates
(c) are given a certificate
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Each of' takes a plural noun/pronoun but the verb that follows it must be singular because the subject is 'Each'. Thus, 'were' should be replaced by 'was'.
उदा. 'Each of' के बाद noun बहुवचन होता है, लेकिन verb हमेशा singular ('was') आती है क्योंकि मुख्य कर्ता 'Each' होता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with 'Each of'

[Q1374] Scarcely had we reached the station when the train left.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) than the train left
(b) before the train had left
(c) then the train left
(d) No improvement
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The sentence is already grammatically correct. 'Scarcely' is correctly paired with 'when', and the verb forms (past perfect 'had reached' and simple past 'left') are appropriate.
उदा. वाक्य पूरी तरह से सही है। 'Scarcely' के साथ 'when' का प्रयोग होता है और Tense का संयोजन भी सही है।
[RULE] No Error / Correct Usage of Scarcely... when

[Q1375] The committee decided to postpone the meeting until the report was finished.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2018]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) until the report is finished
(b) after the report was finished
(c) during the report's finishing
(d) once the report will be finished
[ANS] a
[SOL]
After the conjunction *until* we use the present simple to refer to future actions. Hence *until the report is finished* is correct.
उदाहरण: वह तब तक प्रतीक्षा करेगा जब तक रिपोर्ट पूरी नहीं हो जाती।
[RULE] Use present simple after 'until' for future reference

[Q1376] She asked me to carry the boxes, which I gladly accepted.

(a) that I gladly accepted
(b) which I gladly accepted
(c) which I accepted gladly
(d) which gladly accepted I
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause should be a relative clause starting with *that*. Therefore *that I gladly accepted* is grammatically correct.
उदाहरण: उसने मुझे बॉक्स ले जाने के लिए कहा, जिसे मैंने खुशी से स्वीकार किया।
[RULE] Use 'that' for defining relative clauses

[SOL]
The if‑clause in a third conditional uses past perfect. Hence *if he had studied harder* is correct.
उदाहरण: अगर वह अधिक मेहनत करता, तो वह बेहतर शिक्षक बन सकता था।

A relative clause referring to a noun phrase uses *which*. The future tense *will reduce* is appropriate.

[Q1534] The new policy, **which is expected to reduce carbon emissions by 30% over the next decade**, will be implemented next year.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) expected to reduce carbon emissions by 30% over the next decade
(b) expected to reduce carbon emissions by 30 per cent over the next decade
(c) which is expected to reduce the carbon emissions by 30% over the next decade
(d) which expects to reduce carbon emissions by 30% over the next decade
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase can be replaced by an adjective clause ‘expected to reduce…’. The first option is correct because it removes the unnecessary relative pronoun and keeps the meaning clear.
उदा. नीति, जो 30% तक उत्सर्जन घटाने की उम्मीद है, अगले वर्ष लागू होगी।
[RULE] Adjective Clause – Removing unnecessary relative pronoun

[Q1535] She was praised for her **quickly responding to the emergency situation**, which earned her a medal.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) quickly responding to the emergency situation
(b) quickly respond to the emergency situation
(c) quickly responding to the emergency situations
(d) quickly responds to the emergency situation
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The participle should agree with the subject; ‘quickly responding’ is the correct form of the gerund phrase.
उदा. उसने तेजी से आपात स्थिति पर प्रतिक्रिया दी, जिसके लिए उसे सम्मान मिला।
[RULE] Gerund Phrase – Correct participle form

[Q1536] The manager, **whose decision was delayed by three days**, was eventually satisfied with the out come
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) whose decision was delayed for three days
(b) that decision was delayed by three days
(c) who delayed the decision by three days
(d) whose decision delayed by three days
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Replace the relative clause with a noun phrase ‘whose decision was delayed for three days’. The preposition ‘for’ is appropriate for duration.
उदा. प्रबंधक, जिसकी निर्णय तीन दिन देर से हुआ, अंततः संतुष्ट था।
[RULE] Relative Clause – Correct preposition for duration

[Q1537] The students, **by attending the work shop actively**, improved their present at i on skills.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) by attending the workshop actively
(b) by actively attending the workshop
(c) by attending the workshop active
(d) by attending and actively the workshop
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The adverb ‘actively’ should precede the verb ‘attending’ for correct word order.
उदा. छात्र, सक्रिय रूप से कार्यशाला में भाग लेकर, अपनी प्रस्तुति कौशल में सुधार किया।
[RULE] Adverb Placement – Adverb before verb

[Q1538] The report, **that was submitted last week**, contains detailed analysis of the market trends.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) that was submitted last week
(b) submitted last week
(c) was submitted last week
(d) was submitted the last week
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The relative pronoun ‘that’ is unnecessary; a reduced relative clause ‘submitted last week’ is preferred.
उदा. रिपोर्ट, जो पिछले सप्ताह जमा की गई थी, बाजार प्रवृत्तियों का विस्तृत विश्लेषण रखती है।
[RULE] Reduced Relative Clause – Omitting relative pronoun

[Q1539] The engineer, **with having designed the bridge**, received commendation from the city council.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) with having designed the bridge
(b) having designed the bridge
(c) who had designed the bridge
(d) who designed the bridge
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correct participial phrase is ‘having designed the bridge’. The preposition ‘with’ is redundant.
उदा. इंजीनियर, जिसने पुल का डिजाइन किया, को नगर परिषद से प्रशंसा मिली।
[RULE] Participial Phrase – Removing unnecessary preposition

[Q1540] The festival, **during which hundreds of tourists visit the town**, showcases local culture.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) during which hundreds of tourists visit the town
(b) when hundreds of tourists visit the town
(c) during hundreds of tourists visit the town
(d) at which hundreds of tourists visit the town
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The pronoun ‘which’ is redundant; ‘when’ is the correct conjunction for time.
उदा. त्योहार, जब सैकड़ों पर्यटक शहर आते हैं, स्थानीय संस्कृति को प्रदर्शित करता है।
[RULE] Time Clause – Using ‘when’ instead of ‘during which’

[Q1541] The children, **by being taught democratic values**, develop critical thin king skills.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Dubious
(b) by being taught democratic values
(c) by taught democratic values
(d) by teaching democratic values
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The infinitive ‘to teach’ is required after ‘by’. The correct form is ‘by teaching’.
उदा. बच्चे, लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों को सिखाकर, आलोचनात्मक सोच कौशल विकसित करते हैं।
[RULE] Infinitive of Purpose – ‘by’ + present participle

[Q1542] The plan, **which will be executed after the budget approval**, aims to improve infrastructure.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which will be executed after the budget approval
(b) which will be executed after budget approval
(c) which will be executed after the approval of budget
(d) which will be executed after budget’s approval
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The definite article ‘the’ before ‘budget’ is unnecessary; ‘after budget approval’ is concise.
उदा. योजना, जिसे बजट अनुमोदन के बाद लागू किया जाएगा, बुनियादी ढांचे में सुधार लाने का लक्ष्य रखती है।
[RULE] Omission of unnecessary article

[Q1543] The team of experts, as well as the manager, [were] present.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was
(b) were
(c) has been
(d) had been
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The subject of the sentence is ‘the team’, which is a collective noun treated as singular. Hence the verb must be singular.

वाक्य का विषय ‘the team’ है, जो एक सामूहिक संज्ञा है और इसे एकवचन माना जाता है। इसलिए क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with Collective Nouns

[Q1544] Neither the manager nor the employees [has] been informed about the changes.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) have
(b) has
(c) had
(d) were
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two singular nouns are joined by ‘nor’, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. ‘Employees’ is plural, so use ‘have’.

‘nor’ से जुड़े दो एकवचन संज्ञाओं में क्रिया नजदीकी संज्ञा के साथ सहमत होती है। ‘employees’ बहुवचन है, इसलिए ‘have’ प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with ‘Neither … nor’

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has been
(b) was
(c) were
(d) had been
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The main subject ‘committee’ is singular. The verb phrase after the introductory clause should be singular past perfect: ‘had been’.

मुख्य विषय ‘committee’ एकवचन है। अतः क्रिया वाक्यांश भी एकवचन भूतपूर्व पूर्ण काल में होना चाहिए: ‘had been’।

(a) were
(b) is
(c) was
(d) are
[ANS] c
[SOL]
‘Data’ is a plural noun in modern usage, so the verb should be ‘were’.

‘Data’ को आधुनिक उपयोग में बहुवचन माना जाता है, इसलिए क्रिया ‘were’ होनी चाहिए।

[Q1628] The committee will discuss the proposal **after** the meeting has ended.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) after the meeting has ended
(b) after the meeting ended
(c) after the meeting is ended
(d) after the meeting will end
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause *after the meeting has ended* correctly uses the present perfect to indicate that the meeting is finished before the discussion.
उदाहरण: "The committee will discuss the proposal **after the meeting has ended**".

[Q1629] The company is **planning** to expand its operations overseas next year.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) planning
(b) plan
(c) plans
(d) planned
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The gerund *planning* correctly indicates an ongoing intention. The alternative *plan* would be a noun, not a verb form.
उदाहरण: "The company is **planning** to expand".
[RULE] Gerund usage for ongoing actions

[Q1630] The students were **proud** of their teacher for the award.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) proud
(b) proudly
(c) proudness
(d) proudness of
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The adjective *proud* correctly describes the students’ feeling. *Proudly* is an adverb and cannot replace an adjective here.
उदाहरण: "The students were **proud** of their teacher".

[Q1631] The new policy **was** received positively by the public.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was
(b) is
(c) will be
(d) being
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The sentence refers to a past event, so the past tense *was* is required.
उदाहरण: "The new policy **was** received positively".
[RULE] Past tense verb agreement

[Q1632] The committee **has** decided to postpone the meeting until next month.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has
(b) have
(c) had
(d) having
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The singular subject *committee* takes the singular verb form *has*. *Have* would be for plural subjects.
उदाहरण: "The committee **has** decided to postpone".
[RULE] Subject-verb agreement with collective nouns

[Q1633] The report **was** submitted to the authorities **in** the last week.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) in the last week
(b) during the last week
(c) at the last week
(d) by the last week
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase *in the last week* correctly indicates the time of submission. *At* and *by* are incorrect in this context.
उदाहरण: "submitted **in the last week**".

[Q1634] The committee, **who have** been working on the project for years, finally presented their report.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who has been working
(b) who were working
(c) who had been working
(d) who has been worked
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause refers to a single committee (a collective noun). The verb must agree with the singular subject.
उदाहरण: The team, **who have** achieved success, will celebrate tomorrow.

[Q1635] If she had known the truth, **she would have told** us earlier.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Resilient
(b) she will have told
(c) she had told
(d) she would have told
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The conditional perfect requires the modal 'would have' + past participle.
उदाहरण: If they had arrived on time, **they would have joined** us.

[Q1636] It is essential that the team **arrives** on time for the meeting.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) arrive
(b) arrives
(c) arrived
(d) arriving
[ANS] a
[SOL]
After 'that' in a subjunctive clause, the base form of the verb is used.
उदाहरण: It is crucial that he **leaves** early.
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood after 'that'

[Q1637] The students, **who had studied** hard, were expected to pass the exam.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who had studied
(b) who have studied
(c) who studies
(d) who study
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The clause describes an action completed before another past action; use past perfect.
उदाहरण: The athletes, **who had trained** all year, were ready for the championship.

[Q1638] The report, **which was submitted** yesterday, contains detailed findings.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which was submitted
(b) which has been submitted
(c) which submitted
(d) which will be submitted
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past to describe a completed action in a non-defining clause.
उदाहरण: The book, **which was written** in 1920, remains popular.
[RULE] Simple Past in Non-defining Relative Clause

[Q1639] It is necessary that all employees **keep** their IDs with them at all times.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Zealous
(b) keeps
(c) kept
(d) keep
[ANS] d
[SOL]
After 'necessary that', the verb remains in base form.
उदाहरण: It is mandatory that each student **attend** the workshop.
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood after 'necessary that'

[Q1640] The manager, **who was appointed** last month, has already made significant changes.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who was appointed
(b) who had appointed
(c) who has appointed
(d) who appoints
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past for a past event within a descriptive clause.
उदाहरण: The artist, **who was born** in 1978, is renowned worldwide.
[RULE] Simple Past in Relative Clause

[Q1641] The students **have** been working on the project for weeks, and they will present it tomorrow.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) have
(b) has
(c) having
(d) having been
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The present perfect continuous requires 'have/has + been + verb-ing'. For plural subjects use 'have'.
उदाहरण: We **have** been planning this event for months.
[RULE] Present Perfect Continuous Tense

[Q1642] She would have succeeded **if she had not** been distracted by the noise.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) if she hadn't
(b) if she had not
(c) if she had not been
(d) if she had not be
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correct form is 'if she had not' + past participle for the third conditional.
उदाहरण: He would have won **if he had not** missed the deadline.
[RULE] Third Conditional with 'if' Clause

[Q1643] The scientist, **who has been researching** the effects of climate change, published a new study.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who has been researching
(b) who had been researching
(c) who was researching
(d) who researched
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Present perfect continuous describes an action that started in the past and continues into the present.
उदाहरण: The engineer, **who has been designing** the bridge, will finish soon.
[RULE] Present Perfect Continuous Tense

[Q1644] The proposal, **which was approved** by the board, will be implemented next quarter.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-2]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which was approved
(b) which has been approved
(c) which approved
(d) which approves
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past in a non-defining relative clause to indicate a completed action.
उदाहरण: The plan, **which was finalized** yesterday, is now in motion.
[RULE] Simple Past in Non-defining Relative Clause

[Q1645] During the ceremony, the mayor [politically praised] the local students for their achievements.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) politically praised the local students for their achievements
(b) politically praised the local students
(c) politically praised the local students for the achievements
(d) politically praised local students for their achievements
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase ‘politically praised’ is incomplete; it needs a direct object and an adverbial phrase. The correct form is ‘politically praised the local students for their achievements’.\nहिंदी: 'politically praised' एक अपूर्ण वाक्यांश है; इसमें कर्म और क्रियाविशेषण वाक्यांश की आवश्यकता होती है। सही रूप है 'politically praised the local students for their achievements'।
[RULE] Verb + Direct Object + Prepositional Phrase

[Q1646] The committee had [the meeting] in the after no on.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) held a meeting in the afternoon
(b) held a meeting at the afternoon
(c) had a meeting in the afternoon
(d) had a meeting at the afternoon
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Since ‘meeting’ is a countable noun, the indefinite article ‘a’ is required. The preposition ‘in’ is appropriate for time. Hence, ‘had a meeting in the afternoon’ is correct.\nहिंदी: ‘meeting’ गिनने योग्य संज्ञा है, अतः ‘a’ का प्रयोग करना चाहिए और समय के लिए ‘in’ का। इसलिए ‘had a meeting in the afternoon’ सही है।
[RULE] Subject + Verb + Indefinite Article + Object + Adverbial Phrase

[Q1647] She [is not able to attend] the meeting because she is ill.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) is not able to attend the meeting
(b) cannot attend the meeting
(c) is not able attend the meeting
(d) cannot attend the meeting because she is ill
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correct form uses the modal ‘cannot’ or ‘can’t’ without ‘to’. Thus, ‘cannot attend the meeting’ is grammatically correct.\nहिंदी: ‘cannot’ का प्रयोग ‘to’ के बिना किया जाता है। इसलिए ‘cannot attend the meeting’ सही है।
[RULE] Modal Verb + Bare Infinitive

[Q1648] The scientist [has discovered] a new element in the lab.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]

(a) has discovered a new element in the lab
(b) discover a new element in the lab
(c) has discovered the new element in the lab
(d) discover the new element in the lab
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Present perfect ‘has discovered’ requires a direct object ‘a new element’ and the prepositional phrase ‘in the lab’.\nहिंदी: ‘has discovered’ के साथ ‘a new element’ और ‘in the lab’ का प्रयोग आवश्यक है।
[RULE] Present Perfect + Direct Object + Prepositional Phrase

[Q1649] He [was given] the responsibility to lead the project.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was given the responsibility to lead the project
(b) was given responsibility to lead the project
(c) is given the responsibility to lead the project
(d) was given responsibility for leading the project
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The passive construction requires ‘the’ before ‘responsibility’ and the infinitive ‘to lead’.\nहिंदी: निष्क्रिय वाक्य में ‘the responsibility’ और ‘to lead’ का प्रयोग आवश्यक है।
[RULE] Passive Voice + The + Object + Infinitive

(a) go to the market tomorrow
(b) Futile
(c) Gregarious
(d) Hostile
[ANS] a
[SOL]
All options are identical; the correct form is ‘go to the market tomorrow’. The infinitive ‘to go’ is required after ‘will’.\nहिंदी: ‘will’ के बाद ‘to’ के साथ ‘go’ का प्रयोग होता है: ‘go to the market tomorrow’।

[Q1651] The manager [has been working] for the company for five years.

(a) has been working for the company for five years

(c) has been working the company for five years
(d) Munificent
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The present perfect continuous requires ‘has been working’ followed by the prepositional phrase ‘for the company’.\nहिंदी: ‘has been working’ के बाद ‘for the company’ का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।

[Q1652] The children [were allowed] to play in the park after dinner.

(a) were allowed to play in the park after dinner

(c) are allowed to play in the park after dinner
(d) Timid
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The passive past form ‘were allowed to play’ correctly expresses permission. The location ‘in the park’ and time ‘after dinner’ follow.\nहिंदी: ‘were allowed to play’ अनुमति व्यक्त करने के लिये उपयुक्त है।

(c) designed a bridge which can withstand strong winds
(d) Diligent
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The past tense ‘designed’ is correct, and the relative pronoun ‘that’ introduces the clause.\nहिंदी: ‘designed’ भूतकाल है और ‘that’ संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम है।

[Q1654] The professor [has said] that the exam will be postponed due to the rain.

Both prepositions ‘due to’ and ‘because of’ are acceptable, but ‘because of’ is more commonly used in this context.\nहिंदी: ‘due to’ और ‘because of’ दोनों सही हैं, परंतु ‘because of’ इस वाक्य में अधिक प्रचलित है।

(a) has been working

(c) Impeccable

[ANS] a

The present perfect continuous tense is correctly formed with *has/have + been + present participle*. The verb *working* is the present participle.

(a) would have finished
(b) would have finish
(c) Pensive
(d) Quaint
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The third conditional requires *would have + past participle*. Hence, *finished* is correct.

(a) prepared by

(a) have
(b) had
(c) has
(d) having

In a second conditional, the if-clause uses the simple past tense. Thus, *had* is correct.

(a) that the team finish

[Q1660] He **has** been praised for his dedication.

(a) has
(b) have
(c) had

[Q1661] The students **had** been studying when the power went out.

(a) had been studying

(c) has been studying

Past perfect continuous uses *had been + present participle* to indicate an action that was in progress before another past event.

[Q1662] The new policy **will** be implemented from next month.

(a) will be implemented

Future passive sentences use *will + be + past participle*.

(a) would have visited

[Q1664] The book was **written** by an acclaimed author.

(a) the final report is due

[SOL]

[Q1666] She gave me a book, which [she] had written last year.

(a) she had written

[Q1667] If he had known the time, he [would] arrive earlier.

(a) would have arrived

(c) had arrived

[SOL]

(a) the chairman will
(b) the chairman

[Q1669] He is the one who [deserve] recognition for his hard work.

(a) deserves

उदा. हिंदी में: ‘वह वही है जिसके योग्य प्रशंसा है’

[Q1670] The students were given the opportunity to [participate] in the work shop

(a) participate

(d) to participate

उदा. हिंदी में: ‘छात्रों को कार्यशाला में भाग लेने का अवसर दिया गया’

[Q1671] The company plans to launch new products, which [will] be announced next month.

(a) will be announced

(c) has been announced
(d) are announced
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Future simple with ‘will’ for scheduled events. 
उदा. हिंदी में: ‘कंपनी अगले महीने नए उत्पादों की घोषणा करेगी’
[RULE] Future Simple Tense

[Q1672] Neither the manager nor the employees [were] satisfied with the new policy.

(a) was
(b) were
(c) is
(d) have been

[SOL]
Rule in English: When subjects joined by ‘neither…nor’, verb takes plural form if the nearer subject is plural. Here ‘employees’ is plural, so use ‘were’. 
उदा. हिंदी में: ‘न तो प्रबंधक और न ही कर्मचारी नई नीति से संतुष्ट थे’
[RULE] Verb Agreement with Neither…Nor

(d) the fence still needs

[SOL]

Rule in English: The subject of the clause is singular "workload", so the verb must be singular "is".
उदा. नई नीति से कार्यबल बढ़ाने में मदद मिलेगी, जिससे कार्यभार कम होने की उम्मीद है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement

[Q1761] The scientist, along with his team, has been working on the project, [which will present a breakthrough soon].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which will present a breakthrough soon
(b) which will present a break-through soon
(c) Judicious
(d) Kinetic
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use a relative clause to describe the project; the verb must agree with the singular noun "project".
उदा. वैज्ञानिक, अपनी टीम के साथ, परियोजना पर काम कर रहे हैं, जो जल्द ही एक सफलता प्रस्तुत करेगा।
[RULE] Relative clause agreement

---

[Q1762] She suggested that we should finish the report, but [they have been working on it all night].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) they have been working on it all night
(b) they had been working on it all night
(c) Quaint
(d) Redundant
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use the present perfect continuous to describe an action that started in the past and continues to the present. "They have been working" is correct.
उदा. उसने रिपोर्ट समाप्त करने का सुझाव दिया, लेकिन वे सारी रात से उस पर काम कर रहे हैं।
[RULE] Present perfect continuous

---

[Q1763] The manager requested the employees to submit their reports, and [he said that he would review them the next day].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) he would review them next day
(b) he would review them the next day
(c) Zealous
(d) Pragmatic
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use the definite article "the" before a specific day. "The next day" is correct.
उदा. प्रबंधक ने कर्मचारियों से रिपोर्ट जमा करने को कहा, और उसने कहा कि वह उन्हें अगले दिन समीक्षा करेगा।
[RULE] Use of definite article before a day

---

[Q1764] The article was well-written, and [the author has shown a deep understanding of the subject].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) the author has shown a deep understanding of the subject
(b) Lucid
(c) Meticulous
(d) Affluent
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use the present perfect to indicate a completed action that has relevance to the present. "Has shown" is correct.
उदा. लेख अच्छी तरह लिखा गया था, और लेखक ने विषय की गहरी समझ दिखाई है।
[RULE] Present perfect usage

[Q1765] It is necessary that the students submit their assignments, [otherwise they will miss the dead line
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) otherwise they will miss the deadline
(b) otherwise they would miss the deadline
(c) otherwise they missed the deadline
(d) Futile
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: In a clause following "necessary that", the verb must be in subjunctive mood, but here the conditional clause uses "otherwise" which requires indicative tense. "Will miss" is correct.
उदा. यह आवश्यक है कि छात्र अपनी असाइनमेंट जमा करें, अन्यथा वे समय सीमा चूक जाएंगे।
[RULE] Conditional clause with otherwise

[Q1766] She is the only person who [has been able to solve the problem] in the class.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has been able to solve the problem
(b) Munificent
(c) Nefarious
(d) Obsolete
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use the present perfect continuous for an action that started in the past and continues to the present. "Has been able to solve" is correct.
उदा. वह वह एकमात्र व्यक्ति है जिसने कक्षा में समस्या हल करने में सफलता पाई है।
[RULE] Present perfect continuous

[Q1767] The company had to reduce its work force, [because the market conditions were deteriorating].
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) because the market conditions were deteriorating
(b) Timid
(c) Uncanny
(d) Venerable
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: Use past continuous to describe an ongoing situation in the past. "Were deteriorating" is correct.
उदा. कंपनी को अपनी कार्यबल को घटाना पड़ा क्योंकि बाज़ार की स्थितियाँ बिगड़ रही थीं।

[Q1768] The committee **has been meeting** every week, but no decisions have been made.
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has met
(b) has been meeting
(c) met
(d) meet
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple present perfect when an action started in the past and has relevance in the present.
उदाहरण: समिति ने हर हफ्ते बैठक की है, पर कोई निर्णय नहीं लिया गया है।
[RULE] Present Perfect Tense

[Q1769] She **has been working** on the manuscript since last month.
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has worked on
(b) has been working on
(c) worked on
(d) was working on
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use present perfect continuous for an action that started in the past and continues up to now.
उदाहरण: वह पिछले महीने से पांडुलिपि पर काम कर रही है।
[RULE] Present Perfect Continuous

---

[Q1770] The report **was delayed** because of unforeseen circumstances.
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was delayed
(b) had been delayed
(c) has been delayed
(d) has delayed
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past passive for completed actions in the past.
उदाहरण: रिपोर्ट अनपेक्षित परिस्थितियों के कारण विलंबित हुई।
[RULE] Past Passive Voice

---

[Q1771] They **had finished** the project before the dead line
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) had finished
(b) have finished
(c) finished
(d) Gregarious
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use past perfect to indicate an action completed before another past event.

[RULE] Past Perfect

[Q1772] The manager **will approve** the budget after reviewing the figures.
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) will approve
(b) will have approved

(d) approved
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple future for actions that will happen after a condition is met.

[Q1773] He **was given** the responsibility by his seniors.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) was given
(b) has been given
(c) gave
(d) given
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past passive for a completed action in the past.

[Q1774] The students **are studying** for the exam, which is next week.
[EXAM: SSC Stenographer 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) are studying
(b) studied
(c) will study
(d) studying
[ANS] a

[Q1775] The new policy **will be implemented** next month.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) will be implemented
(b) has been implemented
(c) implemented
(d) will implement
[ANS] a

Use simple future passive for actions that will occur in the future.

(a) has designed and was tested

(c) Kinetic

[ANS] a

[Q1779] The meeting was postponed <u>because of the sudden illness of the chair man / u>
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]

(b) since the chairman had suddenly fallen ill

[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use of a simpler causal phrase. "As the chairman was suddenly ill" is concise and grammatically correct.

[Q1780] <u>Despite the heavy rain, the game continued as scheduled.< / u>
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) though the heavy rain, the game continued as scheduled
(b) although it was raining heavily, the game was carried out as scheduled
(c) in spite of the heavy rain, the game continued as scheduled
(d) while the heavy rain continued, the game was postponed
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The correct idiom is "in spite of" or "despite". Option 3 uses "in spite of" correctly.
उदाहरण: "भारी बारिश के बावजूद, खेल निर्धारित समय पर जारी रहा।"

[Q1781] She has been working at the firm <u>for the past five years.< / u>
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) since the past five years
(b) for the last five years
(c) from the past five years
(d) during the past five years
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The idiom "for the last five years" correctly indicates duration. "For the past five years" is also acceptable but often replaced by "for the last five years".
उदाहरण: "वह पिछले पाँच वर्षों से इस कंपनी में काम कर रही है।"

(c) who had visited the museum after its reopening
(d) who visited the museum after it was reopened
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative pronoun "who" correctly refers to a person. Option 1 is the best choice.
उदाहरण: "वह पहला व्यक्ति था जिसने संग्रहालय का दौरा किया जब वह फिर से खुला।"

(d) postponement of the meeting
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The gerund "postponing the meeting" is the correct form after "decided".

[Q1784] <u>The students were exhausted after the long journey.< / u>

"After" correctly indicates the sequence of events. Option 2 is best.

[ANS] d

The comparative form "than" is correct. Other options are redundant.

(a) The book was sold for a very high price

"For" is the correct preposition to indicate cost. Option 1 is best.

[Q1800] If no substitution is required, select 'No improvement'. Hardly had she entered the office _than the phone began to ring_.

(a) has been adapted

(c) were adapted
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The structure 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb because the subject is 'One', not the plural noun. Hence, 'has been adapted' is correct.
उदा. 'One of + plural noun' के बाद verb हमेशा singular आती है क्योंकि मुख्य subject 'One' होता है। अतः 'has been adapted' सही है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (One of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb)

---

[Q1802] If I _was you_, I would never accept such a humiliating offer.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) am you
(b) were you
(c) have been you
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In subjunctive mood expressing an imaginary condition, 'were' is used with all subjects, even singular ones ('I', 'he', 'she').
उदा. अवास्तविक या काल्पनिक शर्त (Subjunctive mood) को व्यक्त करने के लिए सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'was' का नहीं।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood (Conditional Sentences)

---

[Q1803] She told me that she _has finished_ her home work before the guests arrived.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) had finished
(b) finished
(c) has been finishing
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In past tense narrative, for an action completed before another past action, past perfect tense (had + V3) must be used.
उदा. भूतकाल में दो घटनाओं में से जो घटना पहले घटित होती है, उसके लिए Past Perfect Tense (had + V3) का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Tenses (Past Perfect for prior past action)

---

[Q1804] No sooner did the train stop at the station _than the passengers rushed out_.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) when the passengers rushed out
(b) then the passengers rushed out
(c) than the passengers rushed out
(d) No improvement
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'No sooner' is always 'than'. The given sentence is grammatically correct.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग होता है। दिया गया वाक्य बिल्कुल सही है, इसलिए इसमें सुधार की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (No sooner... than)

---

[Q1805] Neither the teacher nor the students _was present_ in the class room.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) were present
(b) is present
(c) has present
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, the closest subject is 'students' (plural), so 'were present' is required.
उदा. जब दो subjects 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो verb अपने सबसे पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'students' plural है, अतः 'were' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Neither... nor)

---

[Q1806] Despite of working hard, _he failed to secure_ the top rank in the exam.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite working hard, he failed
(b) In spite working hard, he failed
(c) Despite of worked hard, he failed
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. Either use 'Despite working' or 'In spite of working'.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है। 'In spite' के साथ 'of' आता है। अतः 'Despite working' सही है।
[RULE] Prepositions / Prepositional Errors (Despite vs In spite of)

---

[Q1807] He is too weak _that he cannot walk_ without support.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) so weak that he cannot walk
(b) too weak to walk
(c) very weak that he cannot walk
(d) No improvement
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correct correlative structure with 'too... to' is 'too + adjective + to-infinitive'. Alternatively, 'so... that' can be used, but 'too... that' is incorrect.
उदा. 'too' के साथ 'to-infinitive' का जोड़ा बनता है ('too... to')। 'too... that' का प्रयोग व्याकरण की दृष्टि से अशुद्ध है।
[RULE] Too... to structure

---

[Q1808] Each of the participants _were given_ a certificate of appreciation at the end of the seminar.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) was given
(b) were giving
(c) have been given
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Pronouns/determiners like 'Each', 'Every', 'Everyone' take a singular verb. Therefore, 'was given' must replace 'were given'.
उदा. 'Each', 'Every', 'Everyone' आदि शब्द singular होते हैं और इनके साथ singular verb ('was') का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Each + Singular Verb)

---

[Q1809] Scarcely had the minister stepped out of the car _than the crowd started cheering_.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) when the crowd started cheering
(b) then the crowd started cheering
(c) as the crowd started cheering
(d) No improvement
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Like 'hardly', 'scarcely' is followed by 'when' or 'before', not 'than'. Thus, 'when the crowd started cheering' is correct.
उदा. 'Scarcely' के साथ सही कंजंक्शन 'when' (या before) होता है, न कि 'than'। इसलिए विकल्प 1 सही है।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Scarcely... when)

---

[Q1810] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The committee decided to postpone the meeting due to a lack of ________ participants.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) sufficiently qualified
(b) sufficiently qualified participants
(c) sufficient qualifications
(d) Dubious
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use a noun phrase when the adjective modifies the noun directly; hence "sufficiently qualified participants" is correct. 
उदाहरण: "वह छात्र, जिनकी योग्यता पर्याप्त है, परीक्षाएं पास करते हैं."
[RULE] Adjectival phrase + noun

---

[Q1811] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "He is known for his perseverance, which has helped him ________ in the field of research.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) to excel
(b) excel
(c) excel in
(d) excel at
[ANS] d
[SOL]
After a noun phrase such as "his perseverance", the verb that follows should be in the infinitive form with the preposition 'at' when referring to a field. 
उदाहरण: "उसकी मेहनत ने उसे विज्ञान में उत्कृष्ट बनाया."
[RULE] Infinitive with preposition after noun phrase

---

[Q1812] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The manager's decision to reduce costs was applauded, but it also ________ staff morale.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) deteriorated
(b) deteriorated staff morale
(c) deteriorated the staff morale
(d) deteriorated the morale of staff
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The object of the verb is a noun phrase; we need the article 'the' before 'staff morale'. 
उदाहरण: "उस निर्णय से कर्मचारियों का मनोबल घट गया."
[RULE] Direct object with definite article

---

[Q1813] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The new policy will encourage employees to ________ their time more efficiently.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) manage
(b) managing
(c) manage their time
(d) manage themselves
[ANS] c
[SOL]
After 'encourage' we use infinitive with object; "manage their time" is correct. 
उदाहरण: "कर्मचारियों को अपने समय का प्रबंधन करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जाएगा."
[RULE] Infinitive after verb of encouragement

---

[Q1814] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "Despite the challenges, the project was completed on time, proving that persistence ________ results.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) can bring
(b) can bring about
(c) can bring about results
(d) can bring results
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The object of the verb is a noun phrase; we need the adjective 'results' after the verb. 
उदाहरण: "धैर्य से अच्छे परिणाम मिलते हैं."
[RULE] Verb + object noun phrase

---

[Q1815] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The author’s narrative skill ________ the readers from the very first page.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) captured
(b) captured the readers
(c) capturing the readers
(d) capture the readers
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The past tense verb 'captured' correctly describes the action performed by the author. 
उदाहरण: "लेखक की कहानी ने पाठकों को पहले पन्ने से ही मोहित किया."
[RULE] Past tense verb for completed action

---

[Q1816] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The committee expressed its gratitude, stating that the support had ________ the success of the event.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) made
(b) made to
(c) made the
(d) made the success
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb 'made' should be followed by the noun phrase 'the success of the event' without extra words. 
उदाहरण: "सहायता ने कार्यक्रम की सफलता में योगदान दिया."
[RULE] Verb + noun phrase

---

[Q1817] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The new software improved the workflow, allowing employees to ________ tasks faster.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) complete
(b) complete the tasks
(c) completing tasks
(d) completed tasks
[ANS] b
[SOL]
After 'allowing', we use infinitive with object: 'complete the tasks'. 
उदाहरण: "सॉफ्टवेयर ने कर्मचारियों को कार्य तेजी से पूर्ण करने में सक्षम बनाया."
[RULE] Infinitive after allowing

---

[Q1818] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "Her relentless pursuit of excellence ________ her to the top of the class.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) brought
(b) brought her
(c) brought her to
(d) brought to
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The subject 'Her' is the object of the verb 'brought', so we use 'brought her to'. 
उदाहरण: "उसकी सतत प्रयास ने उसे कक्षा के शीर्ष तक पहुँचाया."
[RULE] Verb + object + preposition

---

[Q1819] Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined phrase in the sentence: "The new initiative aims to reduce carbon emissions by encouraging people to ________ greener transportation options.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) adopt
(b) adopting
(c) adopt greener
(d) adopt greener transportation
[ANS] a
[SOL]
After 'encouraging', use infinitive 'adopt' followed by the noun phrase. 
उदाहरण: "नई पहल लोगों को हरित परिवहन विकल्प अपनाने के लिए प्रेरित करती है."
[RULE] Infinitive after encouraging

---

[Q1820] The committee members, <u>who had been invited< / u>, decided to postpone the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who had been invited
(b) who were invited
(c) who had invited
(d) who invited
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use the simple past ‘were invited’ to indicate a completed action in the past that is not a relative clause. The phrase ‘who had been invited’ is incorrect here.
उदाहरण: समिति के सदस्यों, <u>जो आमंत्रित किए गए थे</u>, ने बैठक को स्थगित करने का निर्णय लिया।
[RULE] Simple Past for past completed action

---

[Q1821] She accepted the offer, <u>as soon as she had finished< / u> the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) as soon as she had finished
(b) as soon as she finished
(c) as soon as she will finish
(d) as soon as she finishes
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use the simple past ‘finished’ because the action is completed before the acceptance. The past perfect ‘had finished’ is unnecessary.
उदाहरण: उसने प्रस्ताव स्वीकार किया, <u>जैसे ही उसने परीक्षा पूरी की</u>।
[RULE] Simple Past for completed action before another past event

---

[Q1822] The results were announced, <u>that led to a wave of protests< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) that led to a wave of protests
(b) which led to a wave of protests
(c) leading to a wave of protests
(d) which leads to a wave of protests
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Use a participial phrase ‘leading to a wave of protests’ to modify ‘results were announced’. The relative clause is unnecessary.
उदाहरण: परिणामों की घोषणा <u>प्रदर्शनों की लहर पैदा करते हुए</u> हुई।
[RULE] Participial phrase for adjectival description

---

[Q1823] He was praised, <u>for his outstanding performance in the competition, which was held last month< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) for his outstanding performance in the competition, which was held last month
(b) for his outstanding performance in the competition, that was held last month
(c) for his outstanding performance in the competition, the competition was held last month
(d) for his outstanding performance in the competition, held last month
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Use a participial phrase ‘held last month’ to modify ‘competition’ without a relative pronoun.
उदाहरण: उसकी उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शन के लिए उसे सराहा गया, <u>प्रतियोगिता जो पिछले महीने आयोजित हुई</u>।
[RULE] Participial phrase for non-restrictive detail

---

[Q1824] The project will be completed, <u>if the funding is secured by the end of this year< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) if the funding is secured by the end of this year
(b) if the funding will be secured by the end of this year
(c) if the funding had been secured by the end of this year
(d) if the funding had secured by the end of this year
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use the simple present ‘is secured’ in a conditional clause referring to a future possibility. ‘Will be secured’ is incorrect.
उदाहरण: परियोजना तब पूरी होगी, <u>यदि इस वर्ष के अंत तक धन सुरक्षित किया जाता है</u>।
[RULE] Simple Present in ‘if’ clause for future condition

---

[Q1825] They announced the new policy, <u>which was expected to raise productivity levels< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which was expected to raise productivity levels
(b) that was expected to raise productivity levels
(c) who was expected to raise productivity levels
(d) who expected to raise productivity levels
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use the relative pronoun ‘which’ to refer to a policy (inanimate). ‘Who’ is incorrect.
उदाहरण: उन्होंने नई नीति की घोषणा की, <u>जिससे उत्पादकता स्तर बढ़ने की उम्मीद थी</u>।
[RULE] Relative pronoun ‘which’ for inanimate nouns

---

[Q1826] The students were excited, <u>as the exam results were announced< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) as the exam results were announced
(b) when the exam results were announced
(c) while the exam results were announced
(d) after the exam results were announced
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Use ‘when’ to indicate the time of the action. ‘As’ is less precise here.
उदाहरण: छात्र उत्साहित थे, <u>जब परीक्षा के परिणाम घोषित हुए</u>।
[RULE] Use ‘when’ for time reference

---

[Q1827] He will attend the conference, <u>unless the schedule changes< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) unless the schedule changes
(b) unless the schedule will change
(c) unless the schedule had changed
(d) unless the schedule has changed
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple present ‘changes’ in a ‘unless’ clause referring to a future possibility. ‘Will change’ is incorrect.
उदाहरण: वह सम्मेलन में भाग लेगा, <u>यदि कार्यक्रम बदलता नहीं है</u>।
[RULE] Simple Present in ‘unless’ clause for future possibility

---

[Q1828] The new law will be implemented, <u>which was passed by the parliament last month< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which was passed by the parliament last month
(b) that was passed by the parliament last month
(c) whose passed by the parliament last month
(d) who was passed by the parliament last month
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use ‘which’ for an inanimate object (law). ‘That’ can also be acceptable but ‘which’ is preferred for non-restrictive clauses.
उदाहरण: नया कानून लागू किया जाएगा, <u>जो पिछले महीने संसद द्वारा पारित किया गया था</u>।
[RULE] Relative pronoun ‘which’ for non-restrictive clauses

---

[Q1829] The book was difficult to read, <u>because the sentences were too long< / u>.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) because the sentences were too long
(b) because the sentences will be too long
(c) because the sentences had been too long
(d) because the sentences are too long
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Use simple past ‘were’ to describe a fact that was true at the time of reading. Future or present tense is incorrect.
उदाहरण: पुस्तक पढ़ने में कठिन थी, <u>क्योंकि वाक्य बहुत लंबे थे</u>।
[RULE] Simple Past for past facts

---

[Q1830] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) in the same company
(b) at the same company
(c) to the same company
(d) with the same company
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correct preposition for duration of employment is *at*. Hence, "She has been working **at the same company** for 10 years." 
उदा. "वह 10 वर्षों से उसी कंपनी में काम कर रही है."
[RULE] Preposition for duration of employment

---

[Q1831] Replace the underlined phrase with the correct alternative: "He is the most intelligent person ___ ever seen in this department.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who have
(b) who has
(c) whom has
(d) whom have
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The relative pronoun *who* should be followed by *has* because it refers to a singular person. Hence, "He is the most intelligent person **who has** ever seen in this department." 
उदा. "वह इस विभाग में कभी देखा गया सबसे बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति है."
[RULE] Singular antecedent with relative pronoun

---

[Q1832] Replace the underlined phrase with the correct alternative: "The committee, ___ members are from different states, concluded the meeting early.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) whose
(b) which
(c) whom
(d) who
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative pronoun *whose* is used to show possession or association. Hence, "The committee, **whose** members are from different states, concluded the meeting early." 
उदा. "समिति, जिसके सदस्य विभिन्न राज्यों से हैं, ने जल्दी बैठक समाप्त कर दी."
[RULE] Use of *whose* for possession

---

[Q1833] Replace the underlined phrase with the most appropriate alternative: "The project will be completed ___ the dead line
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) before
(b) by
(c) after
(d) toward
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The preposition *by* is used to indicate the time before which something must be finished. Hence, "The project will be completed **by** the deadline." 
उदा. "परियोजना समय सीमा से पहले पूरी हो जाएगी."
[RULE] Preposition *by* for deadline

---

[Q1834] Replace the underlined phrase with the correct alternative: "The book, ___ I bought last month, is already missing some pages.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) which
(b) that
(c) who
(d) whom
[ANS] a
[SOL]
A non-restrictive relative clause uses *which* to refer to objects. Hence, "The book, **which** I bought last month, is already missing some pages." 
उदा. "किताब, जिसे मैंने पिछले महीने खरीदा था, पहले ही कुछ पन्ने गायब हैं."
[RULE] Non-restrictive relative clause with *which*

---

[Q1835] Replace the underlined phrase with the correct alternative: "There were no signs ___ the train would be delayed.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) that
(b) who
(c) which
(d) whom
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The conjunction *that* introduces a clause explaining the absence of signs. Hence, "There were no signs **that** the train would be delayed." 
उदा. "कोई संकेत नहीं थे कि ट्रेन देर होगी."
[RULE] Use of *that* to introduce a clause

---

[Q1836] Replace the underlined phrase with the correct alternative: "John, ___ is known for his punctuality, missed the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who
(b) whom
(c) which
(d) whose
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative pronoun *who* refers to a person. Hence, "John, **who** is known for his punctuality, missed the meeting." 
उदा. "जॉन, जो अपनी समयबद्धता के लिए जाना जाता है, बैठक में चूक गया."
[RULE] Relative pronoun *who* for persons

---

[Q1837] Replace the underlined phrase with the most appropriate alternative: "The solution to the problem lies ___ a thorough investigation.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIII (2025)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) in
(b) at
(c) by
(d) with
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The preposition *in* is used to express the source or basis of something. Hence, "The solution to the problem lies **in** a thorough investigation." 
उदा. "समस्या का समाधान एक विस्तृत जांच में निहित है."
[RULE] Preposition *in* for source or basis

(b) which
(c) who
(d) whom
[ANS] b
[SOL]
A non-restrictive relative clause about an object uses *which*. Hence, "The proposal, **which** is pending approval, will be discussed tomorrow." 
उदा. "प्रस्ताव, जो अनुमोदन के लिए लंबित है, कल चर्चा की जाएगी."

[ANS] c
[SOL]
The phrase ‘decided to’ correctly shows the action taken by the committee.
उदाहरण: समिति ने बैठक को स्थगित करने का निर्णय लिया। सही विकल्प: ‘decided to’.
Rule: Use ‘decide to’ + infinitive for decisions.

[Q1945] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[in spite of the fact that]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Despite the fact that"
(b) "Although"
(c) "Even though"
(d) "Even as"
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase "in spite of the fact that" is a complex expression that can be simplified. The correct alternative "Despite the fact that" is more concise and idiomatic.
उदाहरण: "In spite of the fact that it was raining, they went out." → "Despite the fact that it was raining, they went out."
[RULE] Expressing contrast with a prepositional phrase

---

[Q1946] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[the fact that]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Because"
(b) "Since"
(c) "As a result of"
(d) "Given that"
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The phrase "the fact that" introduces a clause. A more concise and appropriate replacement is "Given that", which is a prepositional phrase indicating cause.
उदाहरण: "The fact that he was late caused trouble." → "Given that he was late, it caused trouble."
[RULE] Replacing noun phrases with prepositional phrases

---

[Q1947] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[the reason why]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Because"
(b) "Since"
(c) "So that"
(d) "For the reason that"
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrase "the reason why" is wordy. The idiomatic replacement "Since" is a subordinating conjunction introducing a causal clause.
उदाहरण: "The reason why he left early was due to illness." → "Since he was ill, he left early."
[RULE] Conciseness in causal clauses

---

[Q1948] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[in order to]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "To"
(b) "So as to"
(c) "In order for"
(d) "With the aim of"
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The phrase "in order to" is a full clause. The shorter and equally grammatical alternative is simply "To".
उदाहरण: "In order to finish the work, she stayed late." → "To finish the work, she stayed late."
[RULE] Simplifying infinitival phrases

---

[Q1949] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[as a result of]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Because of"
(b) "Due to"
(c) "On account of"
(d) "Because"
[ANS] b
[SOL]
"As a result of" is a prepositional phrase that can be replaced with the more concise "Due to".
उदाहरण: "As a result of the delay, the meeting was postponed." → "Due to the delay, the meeting was postponed."
[RULE] Using prepositions to express cause

---

[Q1950] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[in case that]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "If"
(b) "Provided that"
(c) "In the event that"
(d) "In order that"
[ANS] a
[SOL]
"In case that" is redundant. The correct and shorter alternative is the conjunction "If".
उदाहरण: "In case that it rains, we will cancel the trip." → "If it rains, we will cancel the trip."
[RULE] Eliminating redundant conditional phrases

---

[Q1951] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[despite]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Regardless of"
(b) "In spite of"
(c) "Even though"
(d) "Nevertheless"
[ANS] b
[SOL]
"Despite" is a preposition that can be replaced by the more common phrase "In spite of".
उदाहरण: "Despite the noise, he studied." → "In spite of the noise, he studied."
[RULE] Using prepositions to express contrast

[Q1952] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[because of the fact that]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Since"
(b) "Because"
(c) "As a result of"
(d) "Due to the fact that"
[ANS] b
[SOL]
"Because of the fact that" is a wordy expression. The more concise alternative is the conjunction "Because".
उदाहरण: "Because of the fact that the road was closed, we were late." → "Because the road was closed, we were late."
[RULE] Replacing long causal expressions

[Q1953] The underlined phrase in the sentence can be replaced by the following alternative: "The underlined phrase" is "[as far as]".
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Regarding"
(b) "With respect to"
(c) "In terms of"
(d) "Concerning"
[ANS] d
[SOL]
"As far as" is a prepositional phrase that can be replaced by the preposition "Concerning".
उदाहरण: "As far as the budget is concerned, we need to cut costs." → "Concerning the budget, we need to cut costs."
[RULE] Replacing prepositional phrases for clarity

[Q1954] The students (who are studying) in the library should not make noise.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2026]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) who study
(b) who studied
(c) who are studying
(d) who studies
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English.

उदा. "जो पढ़ते हैं" का प्रयोग सामान्य क्रिया के लिये होता है।
[RULE] Relative clause – Present Simple for habitual actions

(a) tallest
(b) tallest of all

(d) tallest building
[ANS] a

[RULE] Superlative adjectives – No redundant phrases

(a) who were playing
(b) who plays
(c) who play
(d) who played
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule in English.
Relative clause referring to a past action uses simple past: "who play" for present tense. The sentence implies the children were playing earlier.
उदाहरण: "जो खेल रहे हैं" वर्तमान काल में है।
[RULE] Relative clause – Simple Past for past actions

(a) was sent

[Q1965] Choose the best replacement for the underlined part.

[Q1966] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1968] Choose the correct replacement for the underlined phrase.

[Q1969] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

Use commas to set off introductory adverbial phrases.

[Q1970] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1971] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-2]

A restrictive clause should not be separated by commas.

[Q1974] The train will arrive at 6 PM, ___ the passengers will board the carriage.

[Q1975] She studied hard, ___ she passed the exam with top marks.
